catheter-related-bloodstream-infection.evidence: Not checked online; established catheter-infection management principles.

celiac-disease.name: Celiac disease
celiac-disease.scope: Gluten-sensitive enteropathy, malabsorption, iron deficiency anemia, dermatitis herpetiformis, IgA anti-tTG, small bowel villous atrophy, gluten-free diet
celiac-disease.core: Gluten-triggered autoimmune small-bowel injury causing malabsorption or unexplained iron deficiency, sometimes with intensely pruritic extensor-surface dermatitis herpetiformis.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: First-degree relative, type 1 diabetes, autoimmune thyroid disease, selective IgA deficiency
HLA-DQ2/DQ8 susceptibility; positive genotype common and not diagnostic

rows.label: Clues
items: Chronic diarrhea, steatorrhea, bloating, weight loss; constipation or minimal GI symptoms possible
Iron deficiency refractory to oral replacement, aphthous ulcers, low bone density
Children: poor growth/delayed puberty; severe disease: hypoalbuminemia, edema, vitamin deficiencies

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Tissue transglutaminase modifies gliadin → T-cell response damages proximal intestinal mucosa
Impaired absorption → iron/folate deficiency; cutaneous granular IgA deposition causes rash
Fat malabsorption → **vitamin D deficiency** → low calcium + low phosphate; hypoparathyroidism instead raises phosphate

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ While **eating gluten → IgA anti-tTG (or anti-endomysial) + total IgA**; gluten restriction causes false negatives
★ IgA deficiency → **IgG anti-tTG or deamidated gliadin peptide antibodies**
★ Adults: positive serology or high suspicion → **EGD with multiple duodenal biopsies**, even if mucosa normal
Biopsy: villous atrophy, crypt hyperplasia, intraepithelial lymphocytes; high suspicion overrides negative serology

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Lifelong gluten-free diet**: avoid wheat, barley, rye; dietitian, cross-contamination counseling
Pure uncontaminated oats usually tolerated; replace iron, folate, calcium, vitamin D and other measured deficiencies
Dermatitis herpetiformis: dapsone for rapid relief after G6PD testing; diet treats underlying intestinal injury
Persistent symptoms → assess gluten exposure, alternative diagnoses; refractory disease → specialist before immunosuppression

rows.label: Complications
items: Osteoporosis, infertility; untreated disease → enteropathy-associated T-cell lymphoma, small-bowel adenocarcinoma
Dapsone → hemolysis/methemoglobinemia; restrictive diet → nutritional imbalance

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Follow **symptoms, nutritional labs, anti-tTG trend**; persistent elevation suggests gluten exposure
Bone-density assessment in adults with risk/malabsorption; test symptomatic first-degree relatives
No proven primary prevention; do not start gluten exclusion before diagnostic testing

rows.label: Mimics
items: IBS: no objective malabsorption, anemia, or inflammatory injury
Giardiasis: contaminated water exposure, stool antigen/PCR positive
Pancreatic insufficiency: low fecal elastase, **normal D-xylose absorption** (low in mucosal disease)

cervical-cancer-screening.name: Cervical Cancer Screening
cervical-cancer-screening.scope: USPSTF guidelines by age (Pap smear alone 21-29, Pap with hrHPV cotesting or hrHPV alone 30-65), screening cessation, post-hysterectomy
cervical-cancer-screening.core: Screen average-risk people with a cervix from age 21; age, prior results, and cervical precancer history determine testing and cessation.

rows.label: Who
items: ★ **Average-risk cervix present**; sexual history and HPV vaccination do not alter schedule
HIV, immunosuppression, DES exposure, prior CIN 2+ → separate surveillance pathways
HIV: **cytology annually**; every 3 years only after 3 consecutive normal results

rows.label: Start/stop
items: ★ Stop after 65 only with **adequate negative prior screening** and no high-risk history
Adequate: 3 negative cytology/2 HPV-based tests over 10 years; latest within 5
Total benign hysterectomy, no CIN 2+/cancer → stop; supracervical hysterectomy → continue

rows.label: Test
items: Choose one age-specific strategy below; annual testing increases unnecessary procedures

rows.label: IF positive
items: ★ **HPV 16/18 or high-grade cytology → colposcopy**, including pregnancy, <25; others: risk assessment
CIN 2+ even hysterectomy → vaginal-cuff HPV-based testing ≥25 years; older exams: annual Pap

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Postcoital bleeding or visible lesion → diagnostic evaluation**, regardless of screening interval
Under 21: no routine screening; unknown/inadequate history after 65 → continue
USPSTF 2018 final schedule below; later draft self-collection proposals do not replace final guidance

table.title: USPSTF age-based choices
rows: Primary hrHPV or cotest every 5 years

cervical-cancer-screening.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [USPSTF final recommendation (2018)](https://www.uspreventiveservicestaskforce.org/uspstf/recommendation/cervical-cancer-screening); post-treatment surveillance follows established ASCCP teaching.

child-growth-and-development.name: Child growth and development
child-growth-and-development.scope: Normal growth velocity, weight doubling and tripling milestones, WHO/CDC growth chart interpretation, developmental surveillance, normal toddler behavioral variants (head banging, temper tantrums)
child-growth-and-development.core: Interpret serial growth and developmental progress against age, family pattern, and corrected gestational age; a trajectory matters more than one percentile.

rows.label: Definition
items: Weight doubles by 4–6 months, triples by 12 months, quadruples near 24 months
Length increases about 25 cm during year 1; prepubertal height velocity about 5–6 cm/year
★ **WHO charts before 2 years; CDC charts from 2 years** in US practice

rows.label: Interpret
items: Nutrition failure: weight falls first; endocrine disease: height slows with preserved/increased weight
★ Falling **2 major percentile channels**, well child → **diet diary, calorie counts** before labs
Correct prematurity through about 2 years; track infant head circumference

rows.label: Use when
items: Developmental surveillance every visit; standardized general screens at 9, 18, and 30 months
★ **Regression/missed milestones → early intervention**; language delay → **audiometry** before speech testing
BMI-for-age from 2 years; weight-for-length younger; consider parental heights and pubertal timing

rows.label: Compare
items: Tantrums, picky eating, bedtime separation distress → reassure, routines, calm limits; no sedatives
Head banging at sleep onset or frustration, normal development → self-soothing; assess injuries
Preschool restlessness, good function → no stimulants; overwhelmed parent → **parenting classes**

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **One percentile cannot diagnose disease**; stable tracking + normal exam → reassure
Persistent skill loss needs evaluation; never wait for school failure
Short parents, normal bone age → familial; average parents, delayed puberty → **constitutional delay**

rows.label: Adolescence
items: ★ Moodiness, privacy, family detachment, rule-questioning, late bedtimes, good function → reassure, educate parents
Parental-pressure conflict, occasional experimentation, no impairment → not ODD, substance use disorder
Weight worry, stable percentile, normal BMI, regular menses → normal; not eating disorder

table.title: Normal by age
rows: Holds head up; not yet reaching
Sits unsupported; bangs blocks, self-feeds finger foods
Walks; scribbles; non-walker at 14 months normal
Balances on one foot; copies circle
Same-sex parent preference; involve other parent otherwise

child-growth-and-development.evidence: Checked screening ages 2026-10-30: [AAP surveillance/screening](https://www.aap.org/en/patient-care/developmental-surveillance-and-screening-patient-care/); growth facts established pediatric teaching.

chlamydia-infection.name: Chlamydia infection
chlamydia-infection.scope: Chlamydia trachomatis, nongonococcal urethritis, cervicitis, lymphogranuloma venereum, neonatal conjunctivitis and pneumonia, NAAT screening and diagnosis, doxycycline and azithromycin
chlamydia-infection.core: Often silent sexually transmitted intracellular infection causing urethritis or cervicitis; untreated infection threatens fertility and can infect newborns during delivery.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Age <25 years, new/multiple partners, inconsistent condom use, infected partner; perinatal exposure

rows.label: Clues
items: Dysuria, scant discharge, sterile pyuria; friable cervix, mucopurulent discharge, postcoital/intermenstrual bleeding
★ Neonatal conjunctivitis at **5–12 days**; afebrile staccato pneumonia at **1–3 months**
LGV: transient painless genital ulcer → tender inguinal nodes/buboes or invasive proctocolitis

rows.label: Pathophys
items: C. trachomatis: obligate intracellular bacterium; D–K serovars cause genital/perinatal infection, L1–L3 cause LGV

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **NAAT**: vaginal swab preferred in women; first-catch urine in men; rectal swab after exposure
Test for gonorrhea, HIV, syphilis; fever, pelvic pain, cervical motion tenderness → evaluate for PID
Infant conjunctival testing requires epithelial cells; nasopharyngeal testing for pneumonia
Sexually active MSM: annual site-specific screening; every 3–6 months with persistent high risk

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Uncomplicated infection → **doxycycline for 7 days**; LGV → 21 days
★ Pregnancy → **azithromycin**, single dose; alternative when adherence doubtful, less reliable for rectal infection
Neonatal disease → oral erythromycin for 14 days; azithromycin alternative; topical treatment alone inadequate
Gonorrhea suspected or detected → add ceftriaxone; PID requires broader multidrug coverage

rows.label: Complications
items: PID → tubal infertility, ectopic pregnancy, chronic pelvic pain; epididymitis, reactive arthritis
LGV → rectal strictures/fistulas; infant macrolides → hypertrophic pyloric stenosis risk

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Treat partners from preceding **60 days**; expedited partner treatment where legal
Abstain until 7-day course completed or 7 days after single dose, and partners treated
★ **Annual NAAT**: sexually active women <25 despite condoms; older if risk; pregnancy entry; Pap from 21
Retest at 3 months; pregnancy test-of-cure at 4 weeks; neonatal eye ointment does not prevent chlamydia

rows.label: Mimics
items: Gonorrhea: copious purulent discharge, Gram-stain intracellular diplococci; **neutrophils alone** → nongonococcal urethritis, usually chlamydia
M. genitalium: persistent nongonococcal urethritis after doxycycline; separate NAAT
HSV: painful ulcers and external dysuria rather than isolated cervical discharge
Cystitis: suprapubic tenderness, bacteriuria; urethritis → **distal anterior vaginal wall tenderness**, sterile pyuria

chromosomal-and-genetic-disorders.name: Chromosomal and genetic disorders
chromosomal-and-genetic-disorders.scope: Down syndrome (trisomy 21), Turner syndrome (45,X0), Klinefelter syndrome (47,XXY), Fragile X syndrome (FMR1 trinucleotide repeat), Prader-Willi and Angelman syndromes, DiGeorge syndrome (22q11 deletion)
chromosomal-and-genetic-disorders.core: Recognize syndromic combinations of growth, cognition, gonadal function, dysmorphism, and congenital malformations; confirm with the correct genetic test.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Advanced maternal age: meiotic nondisjunction; balanced parental translocation: recurrent aneuploid pregnancy
Family expansion history: repeat disorders; microdeletions often de novo

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Down** (trisomy 21): hypotonia, upslanting fissures, epicanthal folds, macroglossia, single palmar crease, AV septal defect
DiGeorge: conotruncal defect, cleft palate, absent thymus, hypocalcemic tetany
Turner: newborn hand/foot lymphedema, redundant nuchal skin; later nevi
**Williams** (7q11.23 deletion): overfriendly, elfin facies, hyperacusis, intellectual disability, supravalvular stenosis

rows.label: Pathophys
items: ★ **Genomic imprinting**: parent-specific expression; deletion or uniparental disomy can disrupt the active copy
22q11 deletion disrupts pharyngeal pouch development → T-cell deficiency and hypoparathyroidism

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Suspected Down, Turner, Klinefelter → **karyotype**; prenatal screening alone never establishes diagnosis
Microarray: microdeletion; targeted repeat analysis: fragile X; methylation testing: imprinting disorders
Down: assess heart, hearing, vision, thyroid; DiGeorge: calcium and lymphocyte subsets

rows.label: Tx
items: Early developmental services, speech support; repair congenital defects
Turner: growth hormone then estrogen/progestin; Klinefelter: testosterone after endocrine assessment
Prader-Willi: supervised food access; Angelman: seizure management; DiGeorge: calcium and infection management

rows.label: Complications
items: Down: duodenal atresia (double bubble), leukemia, early Alzheimer disease, atlantoaxial instability
Turner: coarctation, bicuspid valve, aortic dissection; Klinefelter: infertility, breast cancer
Prader-Willi: severe obesity; DiGeorge: severe infections and later psychiatric disease

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Genetic counseling**: recurrence depends on nondisjunction, translocation, imprinting mechanism, or repeat expansion
Avoid live vaccines with severe T-cell deficiency; use irradiated blood for profound immunodeficiency

rows.label: Mimics
items: Noonan syndrome: Turner-like habitus, normal chromosomes; either sex, pulmonic stenosis
Congenital hypothyroidism: hypotonia and delayed development; abnormal newborn thyroid screen
Constitutional delay: delayed bone age; no edema or nevi
Rett: girls with regression; MECP2 variant

table.title: Distinctive genotype–phenotype pairs
rows: Short female, webbed neck, streak ovaries, primary amenorrhea
Tall male, small firm testes, gynecomastia, high FSH/LH
FMR1 CGG expansion at X fragile site; silencing
Long face, large ears, macroorchidism, autism-like behavior
IUGR, clenched overlapping fingers, prominent occiput, micrognathia, VSD

chromosomal-and-genetic-disorders.evidence: Not checked online; established genetics teaching.

chronic-kidney-disease.name: Chronic kidney disease and end-stage renal disease
chronic-kidney-disease.scope: CKD progression, anemia of CKD (erythropoietin deficiency), mineral and bone disorder, uremic complications, volume overload, indications for emergent dialysis (AEIOU), vascular access
chronic-kidney-disease.core: Persistent kidney injury or reduced filtration causes progressive cardiovascular, metabolic and uremic complications; dialysis follows clinical indications rather than creatinine alone.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Diabetes, hypertension, glomerular disease, obstruction, recurrent AKI, inherited cystic disease
NSAIDs, smoking and uncontrolled proteinuria accelerate progression

rows.label: Clues
items: Early disease often asymptomatic; advanced disease → fatigue, pruritus, anorexia, edema
Uremia: confusion, myoclonus, pericardial friction rub, nausea or bleeding despite normal platelet count
Labs: normocytic anemia, hyperkalemia, metabolic acidosis, ↑phosphate, low/normal calcium

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Nephron loss → hyperfiltration in remaining nephrons, proteinuria and fibrosis
↓Erythropoietin → anemia; phosphate retention/↓calcitriol → ↓calcium absorption → four-gland secondary hyperparathyroidism
Renal bone disease: ↓calcitriol → **deficient osteoid mineralization**, atraumatic fracture; ↑PTH → subperiosteal resorption

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **eGFR <60** or kidney-damage markers for **≥3 months** establishes CKD
Urine albumin/creatinine ratio, urinalysis, creatinine trend; ultrasound for size/obstruction
Stage by GFR and albuminuria; small echogenic kidneys support chronicity but are not universal
Monitor CBC, ferritin/TSAT, K, bicarbonate, calcium, phosphate and PTH

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Albuminuric CKD → **ACE inhibitor/ARB**; monitor creatinine/K; never combine both
SGLT2 inhibitor for T2DM or qualifying albuminuric CKD/HF, generally starting eGFR ≥20
Overload → salt restriction, furosemide; high phosphate → phosphorus restriction, sevelamer; severe hyperparathyroidism → calcitriol
Iron repletion before ESA for selected persistent anemia; correct clinically significant metabolic acidosis
★ **Dialysis (AEIOU)**: refractory acidosis/hyperkalemia/overload (anuria: no diuretics), dialyzable toxins, uremic complications

rows.label: Complications
items: Cardiovascular death, fractures, severe hyperkalemic arrhythmia, malnutrition
Dialysis access infection/thrombosis; rapid urea reduction → dialysis disequilibrium
Peritoneal dialysis + fever/abdominal pain → first **peritoneal fluid cell count, Gram stain, culture**

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Preserve arm veins; plan **AV fistula** before hemodialysis; temporary catheter for emergencies; early transplant referral
BP/glycemic control, avoid nephrotoxins, renal drug adjustment; hepatitis B vaccination before dialysis

rows.label: Mimics
items: AKI: acute creatinine change; may complicate established CKD
Prerenal azotemia: reversible perfusion deficit without persistent structural injury

congenital-heart-disease.name: Congenital heart disease
congenital-heart-disease.scope: Cyanotic heart disease (5 Ts: Tetralogy of Fallot, TGA, truncus, tricuspid atresia, TAPVR), acyanotic heart disease (VSD, ASD, PDA, coarctation of aorta), hyperoxia test, prostaglandin E1
congenital-heart-disease.core: Neonatal cyanosis or shock as the ductus closes demands urgent assessment for duct-dependent congenital heart disease.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Maternal diabetes, congenital rubella, family history; Down syndrome → AV septal defects
Prematurity → PDA; Turner syndrome → coarctation

rows.label: Clues
items: Poor feeding, diaphoresis, tachypnea, hepatomegaly → infant heart failure
VSD: harsh holosystolic lower-left sternal murmur; ASD: **fixed split S2**, pulmonic flow murmur, RV volume overload
PDA: continuous machinery murmur, bounding pulses; coarctation: weak femoral pulses, arm–leg BP gradient
Central cyanosis: blue lips/tongue, warm extremities → **low arterial saturation**; peripheral: cold extremities

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Left-to-right shunts (VSD, ASD, extracardiac PDA) increase pulmonary flow; remodeling can reverse flow → Eisenmenger syndrome
Duct-dependent lesions require pulmonary/systemic flow or mixing through fetal communications
High neonatal PVR limits VSD shunt → murmur appears/louder over weeks as **PVR falls**

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Preductal/right-hand and postductal/foot oxygen saturation; **echocardiography** defines anatomy
★ Hyperoxia test: little PaO2 rise with 100% oxygen suggests cardiac shunting; echo preferred
ECG and chest radiograph support diagnosis; normal murmur does not exclude critical disease

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Suspected duct-dependent lesion → **prostaglandin E1** immediately; monitor for apnea
★ Tet spell (agitation, softer murmur) → knee–chest, oxygen, fluids, morphine; refractory → phenylephrine or propranolol
TGA with inadequate mixing → balloon atrial septostomy, then arterial switch
Large shunts → diuretics, closure; premature PDA → ibuprofen; **obstructed TAPVR → emergency repair**
Coarctation → repair; post-repair paradoxical hypertension → **IV beta-blocker**; Eisenmenger → **do not close shunt**

rows.label: Complications
items: Pulmonary hypertension, failure to thrive, arrhythmias, infective endocarditis
Right-to-left shunting → brain abscess, paradoxical emboli, secondary erythrocytosis

rows.label: Prevention
items: Pulse-ox newborn screening; rubella immunization before pregnancy; maternal glycemic control
Endocarditis prophylaxis for selected unrepaired cyanotic or prosthetic-material lesions during dental procedures

rows.label: Mimics
items: Lung disease: substantial oxygen response, pulmonary findings
PPHN: elevated pulmonary resistance with structurally normal heart

table.title: Five cyanotic lesions
rows: RV obstruction, VSD, overriding aorta, RVH; boot-shaped heart
Parallel circuits; single S2; egg-on-string silhouette
Pulmonary veins drain systemically; obstruction → edema

congenital-heart-disease.evidence: Not checked online; established pediatric cardiology teaching.

contact-dermatitis.name: Contact dermatitis
contact-dermatitis.scope: Allergic contact dermatitis (poison ivy/urushiol, nickel, neomycin, type IV hypersensitivity), irritant contact dermatitis, patch testing, topical corticosteroids, allergen avoidance
contact-dermatitis.core: Pruritic eczema confined to an exposure pattern; delayed allergy or direct chemical injury, sometimes spreading beyond contact sites.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Allergens: urushiol, nickel jewelry, fragrances, latex additives, neomycin, occupational chemicals
Irritants: repeated handwashing, detergents, solvents, prolonged wet work; atopic skin increases susceptibility
Repeated surgeries, healthcare work → **latex sensitization**

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Linear vesicles** after outdoor exposure; geometric plaques under jewelry, adhesive, or topical products
Acute: erythema, edema, weeping; chronic: fissuring, scaling, lichenification
Irritant disease often burns or stings; allergic disease usually itches
Extensive blistering, facial swelling, genital involvement → assess severity and secondary infection

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Allergic: sensitized T cells mediate **type IV hypersensitivity**; symptoms 24–72 hours after re-exposure
Irritant: direct epidermal barrier damage; no prior sensitization required

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Clinical exposure history and distribution first; review work, hobbies, cosmetics, and new skin products
Persistent or unclear allergic disease → **patch testing**, read after delayed intervals
Skin-prick testing and serum IgE do not diagnose delayed contact allergy

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Remove exposure → emollients and **topical corticosteroids**; choose potency by body site
Face, groin, folds: low-potency hydrocortisone; thick extremity plaques: triamcinolone
★ Poison ivy **>20% BSA** or severe face/genital disease → oral prednisone taper **2–3 weeks**
Cool wet compresses for oozing; antibiotics only for bacterial superinfection

rows.label: Complications
items: Excoriation → impetigo; persistent exposure → chronic hand eczema and work disability
Prolonged potent topical steroids → skin atrophy, striae; systemic steroids → hyperglycemia

rows.label: Prevention
items: Protective gloves and barrier care; fragrance-free products; avoid the identified allergen
Wash urushiol promptly from skin, clothing, and tools; blister fluid does not spread dermatitis
Hand eczema ± generalized urticaria → latex allergy: **strict avoidance**, including intraoperatively; no desensitization

rows.label: Mimics
items: Atopic dermatitis: chronic flexural eczema, personal or family atopy
Tinea: advancing annular scaly border; KOH reveals hyphae
Scabies: nocturnal itch, finger-web burrows, affected close contacts

contact-dermatitis.evidence: Not checked online; established dermatology teaching.

contraception.name: Contraception
contraception.scope: Combined oral contraceptives, progestin-only pills, implant, intrauterine devices, tubal sterilization
contraception.core: Choose contraception through shared decisions about efficacy, bleeding, reversibility, adherence, and estrogen-related vascular risk.

rows.label: Who
items: Anyone seeking pregnancy prevention; adolescents and nulliparous patients can use IUDs or implants
Healthy patient: blood pressure suffices; **no pelvic exam** needed before oral contraceptives

rows.label: Schedule
items: Pills daily; depot medroxyprogesterone every 3 months; implants/IUDs last years (product-dependent)
★ Emergency contraception ≤**5 days**: copper IUD/ulipristal; levonorgestrel ≤72 h, no medical contraindications
Progestin-only pills: daily timing crucial; norethindrone less forgiving than drospirenone

rows.label: Special groups
items: Breastfeeding (estrogen lowers milk volume, protein) or estrogen contraindication → progestin-only or copper IUD
Current breast cancer → copper IUD; avoid hormonal methods
Prior VTE, poor adherence → **IUD/implant** (depot raises VTE risk); older exams: depot, avoid IUD after STI

rows.label: Choice
items: Combined pills: suppress ovulation, improve acne/cramps, reduce endometrial/ovarian cancer risk
★ **LARC** minimizes adherence failures; condoms add STI protection
Tubal sterilization: permanent; counsel regret, alternatives, surgical risk, ectopic risk after failure

rows.label: Contraindications
items: ★ Estrogen: **migraine with aura, prior VTE/thrombophilia**, hypertension (stop pill), early postpartum
Smoking age ≥35: combined methods usually avoid; ≥15 cigarettes/day → absolute contraindication
IUD: pregnancy, cervicitis/PID, distorted cavity (non-distorting fibroid OK); copper: also Wilson disease

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ Same-day STI screening need not delay insertion without cervicitis; prior PID alone permits IUD
Sterilization: voluntary informed consent; no required partner approval, parity, or marital status
After ulipristal, wait 5 days before progestin; backup contraception needed after hormonal restart

table.title: Long-acting choices
rows: Treats heavy menses; atrophy → expected benign amenorrhea

corticosteroids.name: Corticosteroids
corticosteroids.scope: Mechanism, adverse effects (demargination, leukocytosis, hyperglycemia, osteoporosis, avascular necrosis, steroid myopathy, HPA suppression)
corticosteroids.core: Glucocorticoids rapidly control inflammation and replace deficient cortisol; systemic toxicity depends on cumulative exposure, potency, and duration.

rows.label: Use
items: Prednisone/methylprednisolone: asthma exacerbation, autoimmune flares, transplant rejection
Hydrocortisone: adrenal crisis; dexamethasone: cerebral edema; betamethasone: fetal lung maturation

rows.label: Mechanism
items: Intracellular receptor → altered gene transcription; suppress NF-κB, cytokines, phospholipase A2 pathways
Reduced leukocyte trafficking and lymphocyte activation; slower onset than bronchodilators

rows.label: Adverse
items: ★ **Demargination → neutrophilic leukocytosis**; ↓lymphocytes/eosinophils, ↑glucose/BP, edema
★ **Osteoporosis, avascular necrosis**, painless proximal weakness; cataracts/glaucoma, thin skin
Infection, psychosis, Cushingoid appearance; **HPA suppression** → withdrawal adrenal crisis

rows.label: Avoid
items: Uncontrolled systemic fungal infection; weigh benefit before exposure to tuberculosis or Strongyloides
Live vaccines: defer during prednisone **≥20 mg/day for ≥14 days**; inhaled steroids usually acceptable

rows.label: Interactions
items: NSAIDs → gastrointestinal bleeding; ritonavir/azole antifungals → increased steroid exposure
Rifampin → reduced glucocorticoid effect; adjust diabetes treatment for rising glucose

rows.label: Monitor
items: BP, weight, glucose, infections; chronic use → eye examination and fracture-risk assessment
★ Systemic use ≥3 months → **calcium/vitamin D**; elevated fracture risk → bisphosphonate
Rinse mouth/use spacer with inhaled steroids to prevent thrush

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **<3–4 weeks systemic treatment: usually no taper**; longer courses → taper after disease control
Unconfirmed HPA recovery plus major illness/surgery → stress-dose hydrocortisone
Steroid myopathy: normal CK; new hip pain → MRI for osteonecrosis despite normal radiograph

cystic-fibrosis.name: Cystic fibrosis
cystic-fibrosis.scope: CFTR mutations, meconium ileus, bronchiectasis, pancreatic insufficiency, sweat chloride test
cystic-fibrosis.core: Recurrent sinopulmonary infection plus malabsorption, poor growth or neonatal meconium ileus suggests CFTR dysfunction.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Autosomal recessive CFTR variants; affected sibling or carrier parents
F508del is common; genotype determines eligibility for specific CFTR modulators

rows.label: Clues
items: Chronic productive cough, recurrent pneumonia, nasal polyps, clubbing and bronchiectasis
Greasy stools, fat-soluble vitamin deficiency, failure to thrive despite appetite
Salty skin, dehydration with hypochloremic metabolic alkalosis; male infertility from absent vas deferens
Neonatal abdominal distention with inspissated ileal meconium; later rectal prolapse possible

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Defective apical chloride/bicarbonate transport → dehydrated airway and pancreatic secretions
Sweat ducts fail to reabsorb chloride; pancreatic duct blockage causes exocrine destruction

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Positive newborn immunoreactive trypsinogen screen → **quantitative sweat chloride** confirmation
★ Sweat chloride **≥60 mmol/L** supports CF; 30–59 intermediate → repeat/genetic evaluation
Two CF-causing variants in trans or specialized CFTR-function testing resolve uncertain cases
Fecal elastase assesses pancreatic insufficiency; sputum cultures guide respiratory antibiotics
Consider CF despite negative limited mutation panel when clinical phenotype is compelling

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Daily **airway clearance**, hypertonic saline, dornase alfa; exercise supports mucus clearance
Pulmonary exacerbation → culture-directed antibiotics; Pseudomonas commonly needs antipseudomonal coverage
★ Pancreatic insufficiency → **pancrelipase with meals**, high-calorie nutrition, vitamins A/D/E/K
Eligible genotype → elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor; check liver function and interactions
Advanced respiratory failure → oxygen/ventilatory support and lung transplant assessment

rows.label: Complications
items: Pseudomonas colonization, massive hemoptysis, pneumothorax, respiratory failure
CF-related diabetes, biliary liver disease, distal intestinal obstruction, osteoporosis and infertility

rows.label: Prevention
items: Vaccination, nutrition monitoring, salt/fluid replacement during heat or exercise
Infection-control separation between CF patients; family carrier testing and reproductive counseling

rows.label: Mimics
items: Primary ciliary dyskinesia: situs inversus possible; normal pancreatic function/sweat chloride
Immunodeficiency: recurrent infection without CFTR-pattern salt loss
Celiac disease: malabsorption without bronchiectasis

cystic-fibrosis.evidence: Diagnostic threshold checked 2026-10-30: [CF Foundation sweat testing](https://www.cff.org/intro-cf/sweat-test); management established CF teaching.

dementia.name: Dementia
dementia.scope: Alzheimer, vascular, Lewy body, frontotemporal, reversible causes, normal cognitive aging vs MCI, Parkinson disease dementia
dementia.core: Acquired cognitive decline interfering with independent daily function; distinguish dementia from normal aging and mild cognitive impairment by functional consequences.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Advanced age: strongest Alzheimer risk; early-onset first-degree family history; Down syndrome (APP triplication)
Vascular risk factors, prior stroke, Parkinson disease
Anticholinergics, sedatives, alcohol, hearing loss, sleep apnea may worsen cognition

rows.label: Clues
items: Collateral history: missed bills/medications, getting lost, unsafe cooking or driving
Personality, language, executive, visuospatial, memory, motor symptoms help establish phenotype
Abrupt change, fluctuating attention, fever, focal deficits → evaluate acute superimposed illness

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Alzheimer: amyloid plaques/tau tangles; Lewy/Parkinson: alpha-synuclein; vascular disease: ischemic neuronal injury
Alzheimer: hippocampal loss → poor delayed/episodic recall; **nucleus basalis of Meynert** loss → acetylcholine deficit
Frontotemporal degeneration affects frontal/anterior temporal networks, often before typical late-life onset

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Patient/informant history, cognition, function**; MoCA/MMSE support diagnosis, cannot establish it alone
★ **CBC, CMP, TSH, B12**, depression/medication review; HIV/syphilis testing if risk
Brain MRI or noncontrast CT → infarcts, mass, subdural, hydrocephalus; avoid routine PET as first test
Normal aging: slower retrieval, preserved independence → reassurance; MCI: objective deficit, independence preserved
Typical Alzheimer: clinical diagnosis after routine labs/imaging; **APOE genotyping not indicated**

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Alzheimer/Lewy/Parkinson dementia → **donepezil or rivastigmine**; moderate/severe Alzheimer → add memantine
Vascular disease → BP/lipid/diabetes control, stroke prevention; frontotemporal behavioral symptoms → consider SSRI
★ Agitation → seek pain/infection, routines/redirection first; **avoid typical antipsychotics in Lewy/Parkinson disease**
Early biomarker-confirmed Alzheimer: specialist-selected antiamyloid drugs; baseline/serial MRI for ARIA
Parkinson dementia psychosis/agitation → **quetiapine** over haloperidol; clozapine needs agranulocytosis monitoring

rows.label: Complications
items: Falls, aspiration, malnutrition, wandering, caregiver burnout; antipsychotics → increased mortality
Cholinesterase inhibitors → bradycardia, syncope, GI effects; antiamyloid antibodies → edema/microhemorrhage
Parkinson disease: dementia strongest predictor of nursing home placement and mortality

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Driving/home safety, advance planning**, caregiver support; assess decision-specific capacity
Visuospatial deficit, e.g., failed pentagon copy → **no car keys** until formal driving assessment
Exercise, hearing correction, social engagement, vascular risk reduction

rows.label: Mimics
items: Delirium: hours–days, impaired attention, fluctuating awareness
Depression: prominent distress, variable effort, potentially reversible cognitive deficits
Normal-pressure hydrocephalus: gait-first decline, incontinence, ventriculomegaly; tap test may predict shunt response

table.title: Phenotype clues
rows: Insidious episodic-memory decline, later multidomain deficits
Stroke-related or stepwise decline, focal findings
Early hallucinations, fluctuation, REM behavior, parkinsonism
Early disinhibition/apathy or progressive aphasia; memory spared
Established motor disease >1 year before dementia

dementia.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [Alzheimer's Association diagnostic guidance 2024](https://www.alz.org/news/2024/clinical-practice-guideline-evaluation-alzheimers), [NICE dementia](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng97/chapter/Recommendations/); established subtype teaching.

depressive-disorders.name: Depressive disorders
depressive-disorders.scope: Major depressive disorder criteria, depression in older adults, bereavement vs MDD, pharmacotherapy, psychotherapy, suicide risk
depressive-disorders.core: Persistent low mood or loss of pleasure with neurovegetative and cognitive symptoms, causing clinically significant distress or impaired function.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prior episodes, family history, chronic illness/pain, substance use, postpartum period, social isolation
Older adults: disability, bereavement, polypharmacy; somatic presentations

rows.label: Clues
items: SIGECAPS: sleep, interest, guilt, energy, concentration, appetite, psychomotor change, suicidality
Psychotic depression: delusions/hallucinations only during mood episodes, often guilt or nihilism
★ **Suicide risk**: prior attempt, intent, plan, means, agitation, psychosis, intoxication
Youth: **irritable mood** qualifies; academic decline, withdrawal, somatic complaints; not normal teenage behavior

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Multifactorial mood-circuit dysfunction involving monoamines, **HPA hyperactivity with raised cortisol**, and neuroplasticity

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ MDD: **≥5 symptoms for ≥2 weeks**, including depressed mood or anhedonia; exclude mania/hypomania
Screen all adults, even asymptomatic: PHQ-2, PHQ-9 for severity; older adults: **Geriatric Depression Scale**
Interview establishes diagnosis; assess substances, drugs, TSH/CBC when clinically suspected
★ **Ask directly about suicide**, access to firearms, protective factors; questioning does not increase risk
Post-CABG anhedonia, withdrawal, fatigue → depression screen; vein-harvest leg edema expected

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Imminent danger or **severe malnutrition** → **observation, psychiatric hospitalization**; remove lethal means
Mild: CBT/interpersonal therapy; moderate/severe: sertraline + psychotherapy; pregnancy → shared risk–benefit discussion
★ Urgent suicidality/catatonia/anorexia → **ECT**; psychotic depression → ECT or antidepressant + antipsychotic
Alternatives: **bupropion** (fatigue/hypersomnia, smoking cessation), **mirtazapine** (poor appetite, insomnia)
Continue antidepressant ≥6 months after remission; recurrent/severe episodes → longer maintenance

rows.label: Complications
items: Suicide, malnutrition, functional decline, recurrence
SSRIs: sexual dysfunction, GI effects, hyponatremia; early activation/suicidality monitoring, especially age <25
Bupropion: seizures; avoid with eating disorders, seizure disorders or brain tumor; mirtazapine: weight gain/sedation
Benzodiazepines in older adults: worsen depression, sedation, falls → stop, use antidepressant

rows.label: Prevention
items: Safety plan, early follow-up after drug changes
Taper antidepressants to reduce discontinuation symptoms; avoid antidepressant monotherapy in bipolar disorder

rows.label: Mimics
items: Dementia: insidious consistent deficits; **pseudodementia**: subacute, "I don't know" answers, recall improves with prompting
Hypothyroidism: cold intolerance, constipation, elevated TSH
Untreated OSA: snoring, obesity, sleepiness → **mood disorder due to medical condition**, not MDD
Anorexia nervosa: fear of weight gain, distorted body image

table.title: Distinguishing persistent sadness
rows: Waves tied to reminders; self-esteem usually preserved
Pervasive worthlessness; bereavement does not exclude diagnosis
Stressor within 3 months; MDD criteria absent

diagnostic-test-accuracy.name: Diagnostic test accuracy
diagnostic-test-accuracy.scope: Sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV, likelihood ratios, cut-off changes
diagnostic-test-accuracy.core: Diagnostic accuracy: classification performance against a reference standard; distinguish detection ability from the probability that a result reflects disease.

rows.label: Definition
items: TP/FP: diseased/nondiseased testing positive; FN/TN: diseased/nondiseased testing negative
False negatives → low sensitivity, an intrinsic test property; NPV varies with prevalence

rows.label: Interpret
items: ★ ↑Prevalence → **↑PPV, ↓NPV**; sensitivity/specificity unchanged if disease spectrum unchanged
★ Positive above threshold: **lower cutoff → ↑sensitivity, ↓specificity**; raising cutoff reverses
LR+ >10 rules in; LR− <0.1 rules out; **LR 1** → no information

rows.label: Use when
items: ★ Pretest odds = p/(1−p); **posttest odds = pretest odds × LR**
Posttest probability = odds/(1+odds); pretest 20%, LR+ 4 → odds 1 → 50%
Parallel tests, either positive → ↑sensitivity; serial tests, both positive → ↑specificity

rows.label: Compare
items: ROC: sensitivity versus 1−specificity; AUC 0.5 = chance, 1 = perfect
ROC point nearest **upper-left corner** → best combined sensitivity and specificity

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Sensitive negative** helps exclude; specific positive helps confirm; neither absolute
Case-control sampling → PPV/NPV unrepresentative without population prevalence
Verification bias: reference testing only selected results → distorted accuracy

diagnostic-test-accuracy.evidence: Established statistical definitions; no guideline-dependent recommendation.

diverticular-disease.name: Diverticular disease
diverticular-disease.scope: Diverticulosis, acute diverticulitis, complicated diverticulitis (abscess, perforation, fistula), CT imaging, antibiotic therapy
diverticular-disease.core: Diverticulosis can bleed without pain; inflamed diverticula cause focal abdominal pain, with CT distinguishing uncomplicated disease from abscess or perforation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Older age, obesity, smoking, low physical activity; regular NSAID use
Immunosuppression increases severity and can blunt fever or peritoneal findings

rows.label: Clues
items: Left lower quadrant tenderness, fever, leukocytosis, altered bowel habits
★ **Pneumaturia, fecaluria, recurrent polymicrobial UTI** → colovesical fistula
Peritoneal signs, hypotension, persistent vomiting → complicated disease requiring hospital evaluation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Mucosa/submucosa herniate through muscular weak points at penetrating vessels
Diverticular inflammation causes localized microperforation; adjacent vessel erosion causes arterial bleeding

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Suspected first/severe episode → **CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast**
Colonic wall thickening and pericolic stranding support inflammation; assess abscess, free air, obstruction
★ **Avoid colonoscopy during acute inflammation**; perforation risk
Colonoscopy after recovery for complicated disease, alarm findings, or overdue cancer screening; usually wait 6–8 weeks

rows.label: Tx
items: Low-risk uncomplicated disease: oral hydration, analgesia, advance diet as symptoms improve; antibiotics selective
★ Frail, immunocompromised, systemically ill, or complicated → **antibiotics** covering gram-negatives/anaerobes
Outpatient: amoxicillin-clavulanate (older exams: ciprofloxacin/metronidazole); severe: ceftriaxone/metronidazole or pip-tazo
Small abscess: antibiotics; larger accessible abscess, often >3 cm → percutaneous drainage
★ Peritonitis, uncontrolled sepsis, obstruction → **urgent surgery**; fistula → elective resection after stabilization

rows.label: Complications
items: Abscess, free perforation, stricture, fistula; recurrence does not automatically require colectomy
Severe diverticular hemorrhage may require colonoscopic hemostasis or angiographic embolization

rows.label: Prevention
items: Fiber-rich diet after recovery, exercise, weight management, smoking cessation
No need to avoid nuts, seeds, popcorn; avoid regular NSAIDs when possible

rows.label: Mimics
items: Colon cancer: progressive symptoms, weight loss, iron deficiency; can coexist
Ischemic colitis: sudden cramping then hematochezia, vascular risk
IBS: recurrent pain without fever or objective inflammation

drowning-and-submersion-injury.name: Drowning and submersion injury
drowning-and-submersion-injury.scope: Submersion injury, nonfatal drowning, hypoxemia, acute lung injury/ARDS, electrolyte disturbances, observation criteria
drowning-and-submersion-injury.core: Respiratory impairment from submersion causes hypoxemia; prompt ventilation is the central lifesaving intervention.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Unsupervised children, absent barriers/life jackets, alcohol, seizures, syncope, risky water activity
Cold water, prolonged submersion, delayed rescue, underlying cardiac channelopathy worsen risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Cough, dyspnea, crackles, frothy sputum, hypothermia, altered consciousness
★ **Persistent hypoxemia or respiratory distress** predicts evolving lung injury despite initially mild examination
Freshwater versus saltwater rarely changes clinical management

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Aspiration washes out surfactant and injures alveoli → noncardiogenic edema, intrapulmonary shunt
Systemic oxygen deprivation causes bradycardia, cardiac arrest, and neurologic injury

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Assess **oxygenation, breathing, temperature, mental status** immediately
ABG/electrolytes for severe injury; chest radiograph for respiratory symptoms, not mandatory in completely well patients
Evaluate trauma, intoxication, arrhythmia, seizure, or hypoglycemia as precipitating cause
Early normal radiograph does not guarantee normal subsequent respiratory course

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Safe rescue → **rescue breaths plus CPR** if arrest; oxygen/BVM for inadequate respirations
Intubate for refractory hypoxemia, severe fatigue, or absent airway protection; lung-protective ventilation with PEEP
Remove wet clothing, rewarm; immobilize cervical spine only when mechanism suggests injury
★ No routine **antibiotics or corticosteroids**; antibiotics for infection or grossly contaminated-water exposure
Observe mild cases 4–6 hours; admit for abnormal mentation, oxygen requirement, persistent symptoms, or deterioration

rows.label: Complications
items: ARDS, hypoxic brain injury, pneumonia, arrhythmia, multiorgan dysfunction
Pulmonary edema may evolve over hours; asymptomatic wellness for days does not predict sudden delayed drowning
Massive freshwater aspiration → **dilutional hyponatremia**, seizures; rare currently, older exam questions may expect it

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Four-sided pool fencing**, touch supervision, swim lessons, properly fitted life jackets
Avoid alcohol and swimming alone; seizure precautions; caregivers trained in ventilation-inclusive CPR

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cardiogenic edema: primary cardiac disease, elevated filling pressures
Immersion pulmonary edema: swimming-associated dyspnea without submersion/aspiration
Aspiration pneumonitis: gastric contents after vomiting rather than water exposure

drug-eruptions.name: Drug eruptions
drug-eruptions.scope: Morbilliform drug eruption, fixed drug eruption, DRESS syndrome, drug discontinuation, antihistamines, topical corticosteroids
drug-eruptions.core: New medication followed by rash: distinguish uncomplicated delayed hypersensitivity from a systemic reaction requiring admission and organ monitoring.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Antibiotics, sulfonamides, anticonvulsants, allopurinol, NSAIDs; prior sensitization accelerates recurrence
Aminopenicillin exposure during EBV infection often produces an exanthem; not automatically lifelong penicillin allergy

rows.label: Clues
items: Pruritus common in benign eruptions; uncomplicated disease lacks organ dysfunction
★ **Skin pain, blistering, mucosal erosions, hypotension** → severe reaction; urgent hospital evaluation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: T-cell-mediated delayed hypersensitivity; tissue-resident memory cells explain localized recurrence
DRESS: systemic immune activation, sometimes associated with herpesvirus reactivation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Medication timeline**, including OTC agents and recently stopped drugs; examine entire skin and mucosa
Possible systemic reaction → CBC/differential, AST/ALT, bilirubin, creatinine, urinalysis; trend abnormalities
DRESS: compatible exposure, skin/blood/organ abnormalities; RegiSCAR scoring supports diagnosis
Biopsy when morphology uncertain; no routine rechallenge or skin testing during acute illness

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Discontinue culprit drug**; stop nonessential agents if severe reaction and culprit uncertain
Mild exanthem/localized fixed eruption → **topical triamcinolone**, emollients; cetirizine for itching
★ DRESS with substantial organ injury → **systemic prednisone**, specialist-supervised slow taper over weeks to months
Anaphylaxis features → IM epinephrine; DRESS requires inpatient assessment, not antihistamines alone

rows.label: Complications
items: DRESS: hepatitis/liver failure, nephritis, myocarditis, pneumonitis; relapse after rapid steroid withdrawal
Delayed autoimmune thyroiditis or diabetes → follow-up organ testing for several months
Localized fixed eruption often leaves persistent hyperpigmentation

rows.label: Prevention
items: Document culprit, timing, phenotype, severity; provide written avoidance instructions
After severe reactions: avoid culprit/cross-reactive drugs; uncertain allergy labels → specialist evaluation

rows.label: Mimics
items: Viral exanthem: infectious prodrome/exposures; no convincing drug timeline
SJS/TEN: epidermal necrosis and prominent painful mucositis
Urticaria: migratory wheals, individual lesions disappear within 24 h

table.title: Timing and morphology
rows: Usually 1–2 weeks; long-term use does not exclude
Sharply demarcated dusky plaque; identical site

dyslipidemia.name: Dyslipidemia
dyslipidemia.scope: Lipid screening guidelines, ASCVD risk calculation, statin therapy indications, monitoring response to diet and pharmacotherapy
dyslipidemia.core: Excess atherogenic lipoproteins drive ASCVD; treatment intensity follows established disease, severe LDL elevation, diabetes, and estimated absolute cardiovascular risk.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Familial disorders, saturated-fat intake, obesity, diabetes, hypothyroidism, nephrotic syndrome, cholestasis
Premature ASCVD family history, CKD, smoking, inflammatory disease increase treatment benefit

rows.label: Clues
items: Usually asymptomatic; tendon xanthomas/early corneal arcus suggest familial hypercholesterolemia
Severe triglyceride elevation: eruptive xanthomas, pancreatitis; low HDL alone is not a drug target

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Retained apoB-containing particles → arterial inflammation and plaque formation
Statins inhibit HMG-CoA reductase → hepatic LDL-receptor upregulation
Familial hypercholesterolemia: **defective LDL-receptor uptake** → isolated high LDL, clear plasma; high TG: milky plasma

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Lipid panel from age 19, at least every 5 years**; earlier/more often with risk
Nonfasting panel acceptable; markedly high triglycerides → fasting repeat/secondary-cause evaluation; Lp(a) once/lifetime
★ **PREVENT-ASCVD**, ages 30–79, LDL 70–189 without ASCVD: replaces pooled-cohort equations in 2026 guidance
Uncertain statin decision → coronary calcium; zero insufficient for deferral with diabetes, smoking, strong premature history
High total cholesterol alone → full lipid panel before treatment

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Clinical ASCVD (CAD, stroke, PAD) or **LDL ≥190 mg/dL → high-intensity statin**, no risk calculation required
★ Diabetes age 40–75 → **at least moderate-intensity statin**; multiple risk factors favor high intensity
Above LDL target despite maximal statin → ezetimibe; consider PCSK9 inhibitor or bempedoic acid
Severe triglycerides ≥500 → address causes, diet, consider fenofibrate/prescription omega-3 to reduce pancreatitis risk
Adolescent obesity + moderate LDL → **calorie reduction/lifestyle first**; statin only if severe or persistent

rows.label: Complications
items: MI, stroke, peripheral arterial disease; statins → myalgias, rare rhabdomyolysis, small diabetes-risk increase
Baseline ALT; CK only with symptoms/risk; most lipid-lowering drugs deferred during conception/pregnancy/lactation

rows.label: Prevention
items: Mediterranean-style diet, replace saturated fats, exercise, weight reduction, smoking cessation
★ Recheck lipids **4–12 weeks after diet/drug change**, then every 3–12 months; high despite diet → statin
High intensity lowers LDL ≥50%: atorvastatin 40–80 mg or rosuvastatin 20–40 mg

rows.label: Mimics
items: Hypothyroidism: elevated TSH; correct before labeling primary dyslipidemia
Nephrotic syndrome: heavy proteinuria, hypoalbuminemia; treat renal cause

table.title: Risk-based primary prevention and secondary target

elbow-injuries.name: Elbow injuries
elbow-injuries.scope: Supracondylar fracture of the humerus, radial head subluxation, elbow dislocation, fat pad signs, lateral and medial epicondylitis, counterforce bracing, cubital tunnel syndrome
elbow-injuries.core: Age, mechanism, deformity, and precise tenderness separate elbow fracture/dislocation from traction injury, tendinopathy, and nerve compression.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Fall onto outstretched hand → fracture/dislocation; longitudinal forearm pull → pediatric radial-head subluxation
Repetitive wrist loading → epicondylitis; prolonged elbow flexion/pressure, valgus throwing stress → ulnar nerve compression

rows.label: Clues
items: Pain, swelling, limited motion after trauma; open wound or tense swelling increases urgency
★ **Absent pulse, cool hand, worsening pain with passive stretch** → vascular injury/compartment syndrome
Check median/anterior interosseous, radial, ulnar function before and after reduction

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Pediatric annular-ligament displacement restricts rotation; displaced distal humerus can injure brachial artery
Overuse tendon degeneration differs from inflammatory arthritis; cubital tunnel compresses the ulnar nerve

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Trauma/deformity → **AP/lateral radiographs**; posterior fat pad indicates occult intra-articular fracture
Anterior humeral line missing capitellum supports displaced supracondylar fracture
Classic nursemaid presentation without swelling/bony tenderness → clinical diagnosis; image atypical or failed reduction
Nerve-conduction testing for uncertain or persistent cubital neuropathy

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Supracondylar fracture: **splint and urgent orthopedics**; displaced/vascularly compromised → reduction and pinning
Elbow dislocation → reduction, repeat neurovascular examination/films, early supervised motion
★ Nursemaid elbow → **hyperpronation** or supination-flexion; reassess spontaneous arm use
Tendinopathy: rest, NSAIDs, rehabilitation, counterforce brace; cubital tunnel: avoid flexion/pressure, night splint

rows.label: Complications
items: Volkmann ischemic contracture, malunion/cubitus varus, persistent neuropathy
Dislocation → stiffness, instability, heterotopic ossification; immobilization worsens loss of motion

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Lift children **under the arms**, avoiding traction on hands/wrists
Ergonomic tools, gradual load progression, stretching/strengthening; pad elbow during repetitive contact

rows.label: Mimics
items: Septic joint: fever, effusion, severe passive-motion pain
Radial-head fracture: adult fall, lateral tenderness, painful pronation/supination

table.title: Overuse localization
rows: Medial pain during wrist flexion/pronation against resistance

elbow-injuries.evidence: Not checked online; established orthopedic and peripheral nerve principles.

encephalitis.name: Encephalitis
encephalitis.scope: Herpes simplex virus (HSV-1), temporal lobe lesions, CSF analysis (elevated RBCs, lymphocytic pleocytosis, PCR), IV acyclovir, West Nile virus, autoimmune encephalitis
encephalitis.core: Fever with sustained altered mental status, seizures, or focal neurologic deficits suggests brain inflammation and warrants immediate empiric acyclovir.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: HSV-1 often occurs without immunosuppression; mosquito exposure suggests arboviruses
Autoimmune disease or tumor association; anti-NMDA receptor disease sometimes accompanies ovarian teratoma
Neonate, days–weeks old: perinatal HSV → seizures, fever, CSF RBCs, negative Gram stain

rows.label: Clues
items: HSV: personality change, aphasia, olfactory hallucinations, focal seizures
★ **Temporal lobe abnormalities** strongly suggest HSV; hemorrhagic CSF possible but not required
West Nile: movement disorder or asymmetric flaccid weakness; anti-NMDA: psychosis, dyskinesia, autonomic instability
Paraneoplastic limbic: **small cell lung cancer**, subacute psychosis/memory loss, medial temporal lesions, negative HSV PCR

rows.label: Pathophys
items: HSV causes necrotizing inflammation, often limbic/temporal; mosquito-borne viruses infect neuronal tissue
Autoantibodies against neuronal surface antigens disrupt synaptic signaling

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **LP: CSF cells, protein, glucose, HSV PCR**; lymphocytes, ↑protein, usually normal glucose
Neuroimaging before LP for focal deficits, papilledema, marked impaired consciousness, or suspected mass effect
MRI more sensitive than CT; EEG identifies nonconvulsive seizures or temporal periodic discharges
Early negative PCR with strong suspicion → continue treatment and repeat CSF PCR in 3–7 days
West Nile: CSF IgM; autoimmune suspicion → CSF/serum antibodies and tumor search

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Suspected HSV → **IV acyclovir immediately**, usually 14–21 days; do not await PCR
Airway/seizure support; possible bacterial infection → ceftriaxone + vancomycin; Listeria risk → add ampicillin
Acyclovir: renal adjustment, IV hydration; West Nile: supportive care
★ Autoimmune disease → **steroids, IVIG/plasma exchange**, tumor removal after infectious evaluation
Reduced consciousness, status epilepticus, or respiratory compromise → ICU-level care

rows.label: Complications
items: Persistent memory impairment, epilepsy, focal deficits, death; acyclovir crystal nephropathy
Severe autoimmune disease: arrhythmia, hypoventilation, prolonged rehabilitation

rows.label: Prevention
items: Mosquito repellent, protective clothing, vector control; no routine HSV encephalitis vaccine

rows.label: Mimics
items: Bacterial meningitis: neutrophilic CSF, low glucose; overlap requires empiric coverage
Toxic/metabolic delirium: systemic explanation without inflammatory CSF
Primary psychosis: lacks new seizures, dysautonomia, or focal neurologic abnormalities
Rabies: animal/bat exposure, **hydrophobia**, hypersalivation, agitation

encephalitis.evidence: Not checked online; established infectious and autoimmune neurology teaching.

endemic-mycoses.name: Endemic mycoses
endemic-mycoses.scope: Histoplasmosis, blastomycosis, coccidioidomycosis, geographic distribution, itraconazole, amphotericin B
endemic-mycoses.core: Inhaled dimorphic fungi cause pneumonia after geographic exposure; immunosuppression increases dissemination, while morphology distinguishes organisms.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Soil disruption, construction, outdoor work; Histoplasma exposure to bird/bat-enriched soil
HIV, TNF inhibitors, transplant; pregnancy particularly increases severe coccidioidomycosis risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Subacute fever, cough, fatigue, weight loss; nodules or adenopathy may resemble TB/malignancy
Histoplasma dissemination → hepatosplenomegaly, cytopenias, mucosal lesions or adrenal involvement
Blastomyces → verrucous/ulcerative skin lesions, bone disease
Coccidioides → erythema nodosum/arthralgia; dissemination to skin, bone or meninges

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Inhaled environmental spores convert to tissue forms; cellular immunity restricts extrapulmonary spread

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Exposure geography + chest imaging** → organism-directed testing
Histoplasma urine/serum antigen particularly useful in disseminated disease; tissue shows intracellular small yeasts
Coccidioides serology with confirmatory testing; tissue spherules contain endospores
Blastomyces broad-based budding yeast on tissue; culture confirms; antigen cross-reacts with Histoplasma

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Mild self-limited pulmonary histoplasmosis → **observation** in immunocompetent patients
Persistent/worsening histoplasmosis or nonsevere blastomycosis → itraconazole
★ Severe/disseminated histoplasmosis or blastomycosis → **liposomal amphotericin B**, then itraconazole
Uncomplicated cocci often observation; prolonged/severe illness or high-risk host → fluconazole
★ Coccidioidal meningitis → **lifelong fluconazole**; severe nonmeningeal disease → amphotericin induction

rows.label: Complications
items: Histoplasma → fibrosing mediastinitis; disseminated disease → organ failure
Amphotericin → nephrotoxicity, low K/Mg; azoles → liver injury and drug interactions

rows.label: Prevention
items: Dust exposure reduction/respiratory protection; selected profoundly immunosuppressed patients → antifungal prophylaxis

rows.label: Mimics
items: TB: acid-fast testing and mycobacterial culture
Sarcoidosis: noninfectious granulomas; exclude fungi before immunosuppression
Sporotrichosis: thorn/soil inoculation in gardeners → hand papule, **ascending lymphocutaneous nodules**; not inhaled

endemic-mycoses.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [IDSA histoplasmosis 2025](https://www.idsociety.org/practice-guideline/histoplasmosis-2025/); other mycoses: established teaching.

epilepsy.name: Epilepsy
epilepsy.scope: Focal seizures, generalized tonic-clonic seizures, absence seizures, juvenile myoclonic epilepsy, EEG findings, antiepileptic therapy (valproate, levetiracetam, lamotrigine), lifestyle counseling
epilepsy.core: Recurrent unprovoked seizures reflect epilepsy; classify focal versus generalized onset before choosing a maintenance antiseizure drug.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prior brain injury, stroke, CNS infection, developmental lesions, genetic predisposition
Sleep deprivation, alcohol withdrawal and missed drugs can precipitate seizures; provoked seizures alone ≠ epilepsy

rows.label: Clues
items: Focal onset: aura, unilateral motor activity, automatisms or impaired awareness; may evolve bilaterally
Generalized tonic-clonic: abrupt loss of consciousness, stiffening/jerking, postictal confusion, lateral tongue injury
Absence: staring, immediate recovery; JME: morning myoclonus ± generalized convulsions
Infantile spasms: flexion clusters, **hypsarrhythmia** on EEG; standard antiseizure drugs ineffective

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Abnormally synchronized cortical neuronal discharges impair awareness, sensation or motor function
Excitatory/inhibitory imbalance may arise from structural lesions or inherited channel/network dysfunction

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **EEG and epilepsy-protocol MRI** after unprovoked seizure; normal EEG does not exclude epilepsy
Epilepsy: ≥2 unprovoked seizures >24 hours apart, or one with high recurrence risk/defined syndrome
Check glucose/electrolytes and provoking causes; urgent CT for trauma, focal deficit or persistent altered consciousness
Absence: generalized **3-Hz spike-wave**, provoked by hyperventilation; JME: generalized polyspike-wave
Child, nocturnal facial twitching/drooling, speech arrest + **centrotemporal spikes** → benign rolandic epilepsy

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Convulsion **≥5 minutes** → airway/glucose, **lorazepam**, then IV levetiracetam/fosphenytoin/valproate
Focal epilepsy → lamotrigine or levetiracetam; generalized tonic-clonic/JME → broad-spectrum agent
★ Valproate effective for generalized syndromes; **avoid when pregnancy possible** if alternatives effective
Pure absence → ethosuximide; absence + tonic-clonic → broad-spectrum drug; infantile spasms → **ACTH or vigabatrin**
Avoid carbamazepine/phenytoin for absence/myoclonic syndromes; drug-resistant focal disease → surgical evaluation

rows.label: Complications
items: Status epilepticus, injury, aspiration, SUDEP; valproate → hepatotoxicity, pancreatitis, teratogenicity
Lamotrigine → serious rash with rapid titration
Levetiracetam → irritability/mood symptoms; depression history + high recurrence risk → continue, monitor mood
Erythromycin (CYP3A4 inhibitor) ↑carbamazepine → ataxia, somnolence, diplopia

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Adherence, regular sleep, avoid alcohol excess; no abrupt drug withdrawal
Driving restrictions follow local law; no unsupervised swimming/heights; preconception folate and drug review
Pregnancy lowers antiseizure levels; breakthrough seizures → **increase current drug dose**, avoid switching

rows.label: Mimics
items: Syncope: prodrome, rapid recovery; brief jerks possible
Psychogenic nonepileptic events: video-EEG confirms typical event without epileptic correlate

table.title: Focal seizure localization
rows: Epigastric/olfactory aura, lip-smacking automatisms; superior quadrantanopia

epilepsy.evidence: Pregnancy recommendations checked 2026-10-30: [AAN/AES/SMFM 2024](https://www.aan.com/PressRoom/Home/PressRelease/5170); classification established teaching.

esophageal-perforation.name: Esophageal perforation
esophageal-perforation.scope: Boerhaave syndrome, iatrogenic perforation, mediastinitis, gastrografin esophagography, emergent surgical repair
esophageal-perforation.core: Severe chest pain after vomiting or esophageal instrumentation, with systemic toxicity or mediastinal air, is an esophageal emergency.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Endoscopy, dilation, foreign bodies, caustic injury; forceful emesis causes spontaneous Boerhaave rupture
Underlying stricture or malignancy increases instrumentation-related injury risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Tachycardia, fever, dyspnea, odynophagia; neck swelling or palpable crepitus
★ **Left pleural effusion**, pneumomediastinum or subcutaneous emphysema after retching
Hypotension, rising lactate, organ dysfunction → uncontrolled contamination and sepsis
Classic vomiting–pain–emphysema triad often incomplete; absence does not exclude rupture

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Full-thickness tear releases saliva, gastric contents and bacteria into mediastinum/pleura
Boerhaave typically affects distal posterolateral esophagus; contamination causes chemical then infectious mediastinitis

rows.label: Dx
items: **Upright chest x-ray first** for mediastinal/pleural air; normal early film does not exclude → contrast study
★ Stable suspected leak → **CT chest with water-soluble oral contrast** or water-soluble esophagram
Gastrografin study negative with persistent suspicion → thin barium study to detect small leaks
Avoid routine diagnostic endoscopy when insufflation could enlarge an uncontained tear

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **NPO**, IV fluids, IV piperacillin–tazobactam, urgent thoracic/general surgery consultation
★ Free pleural/mediastinal leak (even stable) or shock → **operative repair + drainage**; chest tube inadequate
Contained leak without sepsis → antibiotics, drainage ± endoscopic closure/stent; older questions may expect surgery
IV proton-pump inhibitor; enteral feeding distal to leak or parenteral nutrition
Avoid blind nasogastric placement; decompression, if needed, under specialist guidance

rows.label: Complications
items: Mediastinitis, empyema, septic shock, multiorgan failure; delay markedly worsens outcomes
Persistent fistula, esophageal stricture and malnutrition after healing

rows.label: Prevention
items: Careful procedural technique; prompt evaluation of new pain following esophageal instrumentation

rows.label: Mimics
items: Mallory–Weiss: mucosal tear causing hematemesis without mediastinal contamination
ACS: ischemic ECG/troponin pattern; no contrast leak
Acute aortic syndrome: vascular abnormality on CT angiography

esophageal-perforation.evidence: Not checked online; established emergency esophageal management.

essential-hypertension.name: Essential hypertension
essential-hypertension.scope: Blood pressure staging, nonpharmacologic interventions (weight loss, DASH, exercise), first-line antihypertensive agents, resistant hypertension
essential-hypertension.core: Persistently elevated arterial pressure usually reflects multifactorial primary hypertension; confirm accurate repeated measurements before long-term treatment decisions.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Age, family history, obesity, excess sodium/alcohol, inactivity, poor sleep
NSAIDs, stimulants, oral contraceptives can raise BP; assess before labeling primary disease

rows.label: Clues
items: Usually asymptomatic; headache alone does not establish hypertensive emergency
★ **Acute target-organ injury** with severe pressure → hypertensive emergency; BP number alone insufficient

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Increased vascular resistance, altered renal sodium handling, sympathetic/RAAS activation sustain elevated pressure
Chronic endothelial injury accelerates atherosclerosis and small-vessel organ damage
Older adults: large-artery stiffness (low compliance) → **isolated systolic hypertension**, wide pulse pressure

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Average ≥2 readings on ≥2 visits; confirm using **home BP or ambulatory monitoring**
Rest seated, feet supported, correct cuff, arm at heart level; avoid recent caffeine/exercise
BMP, creatinine/eGFR, urinalysis/albuminuria, lipids, glucose/A1c, ECG assess risk and injury
Resistant: above goal on 3 agents including diuretic, or controlled on ≥4; exclude pseudoresistance
Child/adolescent high oscillometric reading → **confirm by auscultation** before ambulatory monitoring or workup

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **DASH diet, weight reduction, sodium restriction, aerobic activity**, moderate alcohol; target generally <130/80
≥140/90 → drugs, usually two classes; ≥130/80 with CVD, diabetes, CKD, or PREVENT ≥7.5% → drugs
★ Low-risk stage 1: **3–6 months lifestyle**, then drugs if still ≥130/80; updated 2025 threshold
Initial: chlorthalidone, amlodipine, lisinopril, or losartan; albuminuric CKD → ACE inhibitor/ARB (older exams: any diabetes)
Resistant after optimized triple regimen → spironolactone; monitor K/creatinine; never combine ACE inhibitor + ARB

rows.label: Complications
items: Stroke, MI, LV hypertrophy/HF, CKD, retinopathy, aortic disease
Thiazide: low Na/K, gout; ACE inhibitor: cough/angioedema; RAAS drugs contraindicated in pregnancy

rows.label: Prevention
items: Medication adherence, home readings, regular follow-up; assess orthostatic symptoms in older adults
Weight loss: largest lifestyle BP drop, ~1 mm Hg/kg; smoking cessation barely lowers resting BP
BP control: largest modifiable stroke-risk reduction; also prevents concentric LVH and HF

rows.label: Mimics
items: White-coat hypertension: office high, home normal
Masked hypertension: elevated out-of-office only; secondary causes: abrupt/refractory pressure with renal/endocrine clues

fibromyalgia.name: Fibromyalgia
fibromyalgia.scope: Widespread chronic musculoskeletal pain, tender points, fatigue, nonrestorative sleep, cognitive symptoms, exercise, pharmacotherapy
fibromyalgia.core: Widespread pain with fatigue, unrefreshing sleep, and cognitive fog despite a noninflammatory examination suggests altered central pain processing.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: More often women; mood/anxiety disorders, trauma, poor sleep, family history
Can coexist with inflammatory rheumatic disease; persistent symptoms need not indicate active inflammation

rows.label: Clues
items: Diffuse aching for **≥3 months**, tenderness, headaches, irritable bowel symptoms, paresthesias
★ **Normal strength and joints without synovitis** despite substantial functional limitation
Symptoms fluctuate with stress and sleep disruption; fever, weight loss, objective weakness require another explanation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Central sensitization and impaired descending pain inhibition amplify sensory input
No primary muscle destruction or systemic inflammatory process; pain experience remains real

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical diagnosis** using generalized pain distribution and symptom-severity assessment
Historical tender-point count no longer required; diffuse pressure sensitivity may support recognition
Limited CBC, TSH, metabolic testing when suggested; ESR/CRP or CK if inflammatory/myopathic signs
Avoid broad ANA/rheumatoid panels without specific findings; incidental positives can mislead

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Education + gradually progressive aerobic/strength exercise**; start below symptom threshold
CBT, consistent sleep schedule, treat sleep apnea and mood disorders
★ Persistent symptoms → **duloxetine, milnacipran, or pregabalin**; choose by comorbidity/adverse effects
Low-dose amitriptyline may improve sleep/pain; sedation and anticholinergic effects limit older-adult use
Avoid opioids and glucocorticoids; NSAIDs offer little benefit for central pain alone

rows.label: Complications
items: Reduced activity, disability, depression, social isolation; no erosive joint damage
Medication harms: SNRI nausea/BP elevation; pregabalin dizziness, edema, weight gain

rows.label: Prevention
items: Regular physical activity, pacing without prolonged bed rest, sustained sleep management
Set functional goals; address stressors and comorbid illness to reduce exacerbations

rows.label: Mimics
items: Polymyalgia rheumatica: age >50, shoulder/hip stiffness, ↑ESR/CRP
Inflammatory myopathy: objective proximal weakness, often ↑CK
Hypothyroidism: cold intolerance, constipation, ↑TSH; inflammatory arthritis: objective synovitis

fibromyalgia.evidence: Not checked online; established rheumatology teaching.

foodborne-illnesses.name: Foodborne illnesses
foodborne-illnesses.scope: Staphylococcus aureus enterotoxin, Bacillus cereus, Clostridium perfringens, scombroid, ciguatera, Salmonella, Campylobacter
foodborne-illnesses.core: Incubation time and the dominant symptom separate preformed-toxin vomiting from intestinal infection requiring selective stool testing and antibiotics.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Food improperly refrigerated/reheated; shared-meal outbreaks; raw poultry/eggs, unpasteurized dairy, undercooked meat
Infancy, older age, immunosuppression or vascular disease increase invasive Salmonella risk
Improperly chilled tuna/mackerel → scombroid; tropical reef fish → ciguatera

rows.label: Clues
items: Abrupt short-lived emesis without fever favors ingested toxin; inflammatory enteritis → fever or bloody stools
★ **Severe dehydration, bacteremia signs or persistent bloody diarrhea** → urgent assessment
Campylobacter pain may mimic appendicitis; poultry exposure supports both major invasive enteric pathogens
Fish toxins: scombroid → flushing/urticaria; ciguatera → paresthesias, hot/cold temperature reversal

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Ingested enterotoxins act rapidly; scombroid: histamine; ciguatoxin activates voltage-gated sodium channels
Invasive mucosal infection induces inflammation and can permit bloodstream spread
S aureus: **heat-stable** preformed enterotoxin builds in unrefrigerated food; cooking does not destroy it

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Mild brief outbreak illness → **clinical diagnosis**, usually no stool studies
Fever, bloody/mucoid stool, severe tenderness or sepsis → stool PCR/culture including Shiga toxin testing
Suspected bacteremia → blood cultures; report suspected outbreaks to public health

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Scombroid → **diphenhydramine/famotidine**; anaphylaxis → epinephrine; ciguatera → supportive care
Oral rehydration; severe dehydration → IV isotonic fluids; toxin syndromes do not benefit from antibiotics
Campylobacter severe/prolonged or high-risk illness → azithromycin; most mild cases resolve untreated
Nontyphoidal Salmonella: severe/invasive or high-risk host → ceftriaxone or susceptibility-directed antibiotic
★ Suspected **STEC → avoid antibiotics and antimotility drugs**; hemolytic uremic syndrome risk

rows.label: Complications
items: Campylobacter → Guillain-Barré, reactive arthritis; Salmonella → bacteremia, vascular infection, sickle-cell osteomyelitis
Volume depletion → AKI; antibiotics may prolong uncomplicated Salmonella carriage

rows.label: Prevention
items: Cook poultry/eggs thoroughly; separate raw foods, rapid refrigeration, handwashing; avoid unpasteurized products

rows.label: Mimics
items: Norovirus: contagious outbreak with vomiting and diarrhea
Appendicitis: focal progressive peritoneal findings; toxin illness usually self-limited

foodborne-illnesses.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [CDC marine toxins](https://www.cdc.gov/yellow-book/hcp/environmental-hazards-risks/food-poisoning-from-marine-toxins.html), CDC Salmonella/Campylobacter and IDSA infectious-diarrhea guidance.

table.title: Timing after exposure
rows: Vomiting; cream pastries, mayonnaise salads, handled meats

gallstone-disease.name: Gallstone disease
gallstone-disease.scope: Biliary colic, acute cholecystitis, choledocholithiasis, cholangitis, gallstone pancreatitis
gallstone-disease.core: Gallstone location determines the syndrome: transient cystic obstruction, gallbladder inflammation, common-duct obstruction/infection, or pancreatic inflammation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Age, female sex, pregnancy, obesity, rapid weight loss, ileal disease/resection
Hemolysis/cirrhosis → pigment stones; critical illness/TPN → acalculous cholecystitis

rows.label: Clues
items: Postprandial RUQ/epigastric discomfort radiating to back or right shoulder; assess fever and jaundice
★ **Fever + RUQ pain + jaundice** → cholangitis; hypotension/confusion → severe infection
Pancreatitis: persistent epigastric pain radiating to back, vomiting; ALT >150 supports biliary cause

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Cholesterol supersaturation or pigment precipitation creates calculi; obstruction location dictates organ injury
Infected obstructed bile ducts require drainage because antibiotics cannot reliably sterilize a closed system

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **RUQ ultrasound first**; CBC, bilirubin/alkaline phosphatase, AST/ALT, lipase
Suspected cholecystitis with equivocal ultrasound → HIDA; nonvisualized gallbladder supports cystic-duct obstruction
Intermediate common-duct stone probability → MRCP or EUS; ERCP reserved primarily for treatment
★ Direct intervention: **stone seen, cholangitis, or bilirubin >4 mg/dL plus dilated duct**
Post-cholecystectomy jaundice + dilated ducts → retained stone/duct injury → **ERCP**; HIDA only for bile leak

rows.label: Tx
items: Analgesia, fluids, antiemetics; infection → ceftriaxone/metronidazole or piperacillin/tazobactam
★ **Cholangitis → urgent biliary drainage**, immediately after stabilization if shock; do not await antibiotic response
Poor surgical candidate with acute cholecystitis → percutaneous cholecystostomy
★ Gallstone pancreatitis → supportive care, early oral feeding; **no urgent ERCP without cholangitis/persistent obstruction**

rows.label: Complications
items: Empyema, gangrene, perforation, abscess, septic shock; pancreatitis → necrosis/organ failure
Cholecystoenteric fistula → gallstone ileus; imaging: bowel obstruction, pneumobilia, ectopic stone
ERCP → pancreatitis/bleeding/perforation

rows.label: Prevention
items: Maintain healthy weight; avoid rapid weight loss; selected bariatric patients → ursodiol prophylaxis
After duct clearance → cholecystectomy; after mild biliary pancreatitis → same-admission cholecystectomy
Asymptomatic uncomplicated stones → observation; no routine prophylactic surgery

rows.label: Mimics
items: Hepatitis: marked aminotransferase elevation, no obstructing stone
PUD: burning epigastric pain, ulcer on endoscopy
Inferior MI: ischemic ECG/troponin changes, cardiovascular risk

table.title: Localizing obstruction
rows: Persistent >6 hours, Murphy sign, wall thickening
Cholestatic labs, duct stone/dilation; no infection
ERCP extraction or operative duct clearance
Inflamed gallbladder without stones; critically ill

gastrointestinal-perforation.name: Gastrointestinal perforation
gastrointestinal-perforation.scope: Gastroduodenal perforation, bowel perforation (diverticular, appendiceal, iatrogenic), pneumoperitoneum (subdiaphragmatic free air), acute peritonitis, IV antibiotics, emergent exploratory laparotomy
gastrointestinal-perforation.core: Abrupt severe abdominal pain with guarding, rigidity, and free intraperitoneal air suggests a perforated viscus requiring rapid resuscitation and source control.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Peptic ulcer disease, NSAIDs, H. pylori; diverticulitis, appendicitis, obstruction, ischemia, malignancy
Recent endoscopy/surgery, penetrating/blunt trauma; glucocorticoids/immunosuppression can blunt peritoneal findings

rows.label: Clues
items: Fever, tachycardia, absent bowel sounds, distension; pain with movement/cough
★ **Hypotension, confusion, oliguria, elevated lactate** → septic shock/organ hypoperfusion
Retroperitoneal or contained leaks may lack diffuse rigidity or visible free air

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Luminal contents spill into peritoneum → chemical inflammation followed by bacterial infection and sepsis
Fluid sequestration and vasodilation reduce effective circulating volume

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Stable patient → **CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast** to localize leak and abscess
Upright chest radiograph: subdiaphragmatic free air; negative film does not exclude perforation
CBC, metabolic panel, lactate, blood cultures if septic, type/crossmatch; pregnancy test when relevant
★ **Unstable with generalized peritonitis → surgery**, without delaying for CT
