★ **Hypotension + distended neck veins + unilateral absent breath sounds** → tension; tracheal deviation is late
Ventilated: positive pressure converts occult pneumothorax to tension; sudden desaturation, rising airway pressure, collapse

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Loss of negative pleural pressure permits lung collapse
One-way air entry increases intrathoracic pressure, reducing venous return and causing obstructive shock

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Unstable tension suspicion → **clinical diagnosis; no imaging delay**
Stable → upright chest radiograph: visceral pleural line with absent peripheral markings
Bedside ultrasound: absent sliding/B-lines supports; lung point highly specific; absent sliding alone nonspecific
CT for uncertain/complex cases; supine radiograph may show deep sulcus rather than apical air

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Tension → **immediate needle or finger thoracostomy**, then chest tube; oxygen and resuscitation
Needle commonly fourth/fifth intercostal space anterior/midaxillary, or second midclavicular; insert above rib
★ Minimal symptoms, stable: primary (any size) or small iatrogenic → **observation**, reliable follow-up
Symptomatic/large primary → aspiration or small-bore chest tube; secondary generally admit, drain if symptomatic/significant
Persistent air leak, recurrence, bilateral disease, or high-risk occupation → VATS bleb treatment/pleurodesis

rows.label: Complications
items: Respiratory failure, tension progression, recurrence; reexpansion pulmonary edema after drainage
Chest tube → bleeding, infection, organ injury; blocked/clamped drain may recreate tension

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Smoking cessation**; avoid flying until radiographic resolution and clearance
Scuba diving contraindicated without specialist assessment/definitive prevention; counsel recurrence warning symptoms

rows.label: Mimics
items: PE: pleuritic pain with preserved lung sliding, embolic risk
Giant bulla: intraparenchymal thin wall; CT if stable uncertainty before tube
Tamponade: shock with pericardial fluid rather than unilateral absent ventilation
Massive hemothorax: dullness, collapsed neck veins rather than distended

pneumothorax.evidence: Conservative care checked 2026-10-30: [BTS pleural guideline 2023](https://doi.org/10.1136/thorax-2022-219784); tension rescue: established emergency teaching.

polycystic-ovary-syndrome.name: Polycystic ovary syndrome
polycystic-ovary-syndrome.scope: Rotterdam criteria (hyperandrogenism, ovulatory dysfunction, polycystic ovaries), metabolic risks, weight loss, oral contraceptives, ovulation induction (letrozole, clomiphene)
polycystic-ovary-syndrome.core: Hyperandrogenism and chronic ovulatory dysfunction after exclusion of alternative causes suggest PCOS; management follows metabolic, menstrual and fertility priorities.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Family history, insulin resistance and obesity; lean patients can also have PCOS
Pubertal transition can mimic disease, requiring stricter adolescent diagnostic criteria

rows.label: Clues
items: Irregular/infrequent menses, episodic heavy bleeding, infertility, hirsutism, acne or androgenic alopecia
Acanthosis nigricans suggests hyperinsulinemia; obesity is supportive, not required
Rapid virilization, deep voice or markedly elevated androgens → investigate tumor rather than assume PCOS

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Insulin resistance and ovarian androgen excess impair follicular maturation and ovulation
Absent cyclic progesterone permits persistent estrogen-driven endometrial proliferation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Adults: **2 of 3 Rotterdam** features—hyperandrogenism, ovulatory dysfunction, polycystic ovarian morphology
Exclude mimics: **hCG, TSH, prolactin, morning 17-hydroxyprogesterone**; latter screens nonclassic CAH
Total/free testosterone; **clinical hirsutism/acne** suffices despite normal levels; DHEAS if adrenal source suspected
★ Irregular cycles plus hyperandrogenism → **ultrasound not required**; LH:FSH ratio not diagnostic
BP, lipid profile and **oral glucose tolerance test** assess metabolic risk; adolescent diagnosis avoids ultrasound criteria

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Lifestyle/weight management first for all; modest weight loss can restore ovulation in overweight patients
★ No pregnancy desired → **combined OCP** for cycles/androgen symptoms; cyclic progestin or LNG-IUD protects endometrium
Persistent hirsutism → spironolactone with reliable contraception; allow months for hair response
Metabolic risk/insulin resistance → metformin; less effective than OCP for androgen symptoms
★ Anovulatory infertility → **letrozole first-line**; clomiphene alternative, older exams may expect it; check other factors

rows.label: Complications
items: Endometrial hyperplasia/cancer, infertility, type 2 diabetes, dyslipidemia, OSA and depression
Pregnancy → increased gestational diabetes and hypertensive-disorder risk
Gonadotropin ovulation induction → high multiple-gestation risk, so letrozole/clomiphene first

rows.label: Prevention
items: Regular progestin exposure for prolonged amenorrhea; persistent abnormal bleeding → endometrial assessment
Periodic glycemic/BP/lipid reassessment; preconception metabolic optimization and folate

rows.label: Mimics
items: Androgen-secreting tumor: rapid progression, severe virilization
Nonclassic CAH: elevated 17-hydroxyprogesterone
Functional hypothalamic amenorrhea: low estrogen with exercise/energy deficit

postpartum-care.name: Postpartum care
postpartum-care.scope: Normal puerperal changes, lochia, uterine involution, perineal and cesarean wound healing, breastfeeding, postpartum depression screening, routine postpartum visit
postpartum-care.core: Postpartum care is an ongoing assessment of recovery, mood, infant feeding, contraception, and chronic disease after every birth.

rows.label: Who
items: ★ All postpartum patients; assess support, sleep, safety, sexual health, and reproductive goals

rows.label: Start/stop
items: ★ Contact within **3 weeks**; comprehensive visit by **12 weeks**, with earlier risk-based review
Hypertensive disorder → BP within 7–10 days; severe hypertension → within 72 hours

rows.label: Test
items: ★ Edinburgh or PHQ-9 depression screen; assess suicidality directly after positive self-harm response
BP, bleeding, fundal tenderness; inspect perineum/incision for erythema, drainage, separation
Observe latch/milk transfer; frequent feeds, lactation support; cracked nipples → correct positioning

rows.label: IF positive
items: ★ Heavy bleeding (pad soaked <1 hour), fever, dyspnea, severe headache → urgent evaluation
Mood screen positive → diagnostic interview, psychotherapy/SSRI; psychosis → emergency hospitalization
Increasing wound pain/purulence → evaluate infection; breast fluctuance → ultrasound for abscess

rows.label: Traps
items: Ovulation may precede first period; discuss contraception before discharge
Lactational contraception: amenorrhea, exclusive frequent breastfeeding, infant <6 months
Postpartum hypertension and cardiomyopathy can first appear after discharge

table.title: Expected recovery
rows: Red rubra → pink serosa → white/yellow alba
Descends daily; near prepregnancy size by 6 weeks
Pain improves; pulling normal if intact; keep clean
Early cramping and fluid loss; breastfeeding intensifies cramping

postpartum-care.evidence: Visit timing checked 2026-10-30: [ACOG postpartum care](https://www.acog.org/clinical/clinical-guidance/committee-opinion/articles/2018/05/optimizing-postpartum-care); normal physiology established teaching.

postpartum-hemorrhage.name: Postpartum hemorrhage
postpartum-hemorrhage.scope: Primary postpartum hemorrhage (uterine atony, lacerations, retained placenta, coagulopathy), secondary postpartum hemorrhage (retained products of conception, endometritis), barrier methods, surgical management
postpartum-hemorrhage.core: Excessive bleeding after delivery demands simultaneous resuscitation and cause-directed control: Tone, Trauma, Tissue and Thrombin.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Uterine overdistention, prolonged/augmented labor, chorioamnionitis, magnesium, prior PPH → atony
Operative delivery → trauma; placenta accreta/retention → tissue; abruption/sepsis → coagulopathy

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Boggy enlarged uterus** → atony; firm uterus with bleeding → laceration or other cause
Jagged/incomplete placenta, vessels to membrane edge (**succenturiate lobe**) → retained tissue; oozing → coagulopathy
Shock exceeding visible loss → concealed hematoma; post-cesarean distention, hematocrit drop → **intra-abdominal hemorrhage**
Delayed bleeding >24 hours to weeks postpartum → retained products, endometritis or subinvolution

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Myometrial contraction compresses placental-bed vessels; failed contraction or disrupted tissue prevents hemostasis
Vulvar hematoma: **pudendal artery** branch, often operative delivery; vaginal/uterine arteries → deep or retroperitoneal

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Quantify blood loss; US definition **≥1000 mL or hypovolemia within 24 hours**, regardless of route
WHO 2025 earlier treatment trigger: ≥500 mL, or ≥300 mL with abnormal hemodynamic signs
Assess uterine tone, inspect birth canal/placenta; CBC, coagulation studies, fibrinogen and crossmatch
Ultrasound for suspected retained products; avoid delaying control in active unstable bleeding
Inversion: round fleshy introitus mass after cord traction, absent abdominal fundus, shock

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Hemorrhage team, two large IVs, warmed balanced blood resuscitation; massage, empty bladder, **oxytocin**
★ **Tranexamic acid within 3 hours** alongside first-response treatment
Refractory atony → **balloon/vacuum**, embolization if stable; compression sutures/arterial ligation or hysterectomy
Laceration → repair; retained tissue → evacuation; inversion → manual replacement before uterotonics
Endometritis → **clindamycin + gentamicin**

rows.label: Complications
items: DIC, AKI, shock, death; severe ischemia → Sheehan syndrome
Transfusion complications and hysterectomy-related fertility loss; delayed anemia impairs recovery

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Prophylactic **oxytocin after delivery**, active third-stage management and antenatal anemia treatment
Risk assessment, blood availability and team readiness; routine prophylactic TXA not recommended for vaginal birth

rows.label: Mimics
items: Amniotic fluid embolism: sudden hypoxia/collapse with DIC
Pulmonary embolism: hypoxia/chest pain without primary uterine blood loss

postpartum-mood-disorders.name: Postpartum mood disorders
postpartum-mood-disorders.scope: Postpartum blues (onset <2 weeks, self-limited, reassurance), postpartum depression (MDD criteria, Edinburgh screening, SSRIs, psychotherapy), postpartum psychosis (delusions, infanticide risk, emergent hospitalization)
postpartum-mood-disorders.core: After birth, distinguish transient tearfulness from sustained depressive illness and from psychosis threatening maternal or infant safety.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prior depression/postpartum depression, anxiety, poor support, trauma, sleep loss, pregnancy complications
★ **Bipolar disorder or previous postpartum psychosis** → especially high psychosis recurrence risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Anhedonia, guilt, impaired bonding/function, appetite/sleep changes beyond infant-care demands
★ **Suicidality, command hallucinations, infant-focused delusions**, confusion, mania → emergency
Unwanted distressing intrusive thoughts with preserved insight differ from fixed psychotic beliefs

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Hormonal withdrawal, circadian disruption, and psychosocial stress interact with mood-disorder vulnerability
Postpartum psychosis frequently represents a bipolar-spectrum episode rather than schizophrenia

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale or PHQ-9** screens; positive result requires diagnostic interview
MDD: ≥5 symptoms including depressed mood/anhedonia, ≥2 weeks, clinically significant impairment
★ Screen for **bipolar disorder before antidepressants**; assess suicide/infant-harm intent, access, supervision
Check TSH/CBC for suggestive medical mimics; mania/psychosis → urgent psychiatric assessment

rows.label: Tx
items: Ensure safe infant care, assess support, address sleep; do not leave psychotic patient alone with infant
Depression: CBT/interpersonal psychotherapy; moderate/severe → SSRI, often sertraline during breastfeeding
Severe postpartum depression: specialist-directed zuranolone or other treatment; weigh sedation and feeding considerations
Psychosis: inpatient antipsychotic ± lithium; ECT for severe, catatonic, suicidal, or refractory illness

rows.label: Complications
items: Suicide, infanticide, impaired attachment/child development, recurrent depressive or bipolar episodes

rows.label: Prevention
items: Protect sleep, mobilize family support; prior severe illness → antenatal psychiatric plan and postpartum prophylaxis
Repeat mood screening through pregnancy/postpartum; establish follow-up before discharge

rows.label: Mimics
items: Postpartum thyroiditis: biochemical thyroid dysfunction with systemic features
Normal adjustment: transient stress without pervasive anhedonia or sustained impairment

table.title: Course and disposition
rows: Persistent symptoms; may occur throughout first year
Outpatient treatment if safe; escalate for severity
Emergency hospitalization; protect mother and infant

postpartum-mood-disorders.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [ACOG screening](https://www.acog.org/programs/perinatal-mental-health/patient-screening), [2026 zuranolone update](https://doi.org/10.1097/AOG.0000000000006093); other management established teaching.

potassium-disorders.name: Potassium disorders
potassium-disorders.scope: Hyperkalemia, hypokalemia, cardiac membrane stabilization, shift therapy, elimination
potassium-disorders.core: Potassium abnormalities can cause weakness and fatal arrhythmias; stabilize cardiac risk while identifying the cause and correcting total-body balance.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Hyperkalemia: AKI/CKD, RAAS blockers, potassium-sparing diuretics, tissue lysis, insulin deficiency
Hypokalemia: GI losses, loop/thiazide diuretics, hyperaldosteronism, insulin/beta-agonists, magnesium depletion

rows.label: Clues
items: Flaccid weakness, paralysis, palpitations; symptoms may be absent despite dangerous levels
★ **K ≥6.5 mmol/L, ECG changes, or rapid rise** → emergency; normal ECG not reassuring
Bradycardia/high-degree AV block with renal failure → suspect hyperkalemia; calcium before pacemaker

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Extracellular K changes alter membrane excitability and cardiac conduction
Acidosis/insulin deficiency shift K outward; intracellular shifts can coexist with severe total-body depletion

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **ECG + repeat potassium**, creatinine, glucose, bicarbonate, magnesium; assess drugs and acid-base status
Hemolysis, thrombocytosis/leukocytosis → pseudohyperkalemia; repeat atraumatic draw if clinically compatible
Hypokalemia: urine K distinguishes renal wasting from extrarenal loss; interpret with BP/acid-base pattern
Do not delay treatment for confirmatory blood draw when malignant ECG changes present

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Hyperkalemic ECG changes or dialysis-patient arrest → **IV calcium gluconate/chloride first**; protects myocardium only
★ Shift K inward: **IV insulin + dextrose**, nebulized albuterol; bicarbonate mainly with significant acidosis
Remove K: loop diuretic if urine output, selected binders; urgent dialysis for severe refractory/renal-failure cases
Mild/stable hypokalemia → oral KCl; <2.5, arrhythmia, paralysis, or no oral access → monitored IV replacement
★ **Correct magnesium deficiency** for refractory low K; never give IV potassium push; monitor glucose after insulin

rows.label: Complications
items: Ventricular arrhythmia, cardiac arrest, respiratory muscle failure
Overcorrection, rebound dyskalemia; insulin-induced hypoglycemia; IV potassium extravasation/phlebitis
Diuretic hypokalemia → **digoxin toxicity**, multifocal PVCs; check K first

rows.label: Prevention
items: Review supplements/salt substitutes; monitor K/creatinine after diuretic or RAAS-drug changes
Treat diarrhea/vomiting and underlying mineralocorticoid disorders; replace ongoing losses

rows.label: Mimics
items: Guillain-Barré: ascending areflexic weakness without explanatory electrolyte pattern
Periodic paralysis: episodic shifts, sometimes thyrotoxicosis; avoid excessive replacement causing rebound

table.title: ECG patterns
rows: Peaked T → PR prolongation → wide QRS/sine-wave
Flat T, ST depression, prominent U waves

potassium-disorders.evidence: Not checked online; established electrolyte emergency principles.

preterm-labor.name: Preterm labor
preterm-labor.scope: Preterm labor (<37 weeks), cervical insufficiency, tocolysis (indomethacin, nifedipine), antenatal corticosteroids (betamethasone), magnesium sulfate for neuroprotection, GBS chemoprophylaxis
preterm-labor.core: Regular contractions with cervical change before 37 weeks; briefly delay eligible early births to improve neonatal outcomes, without prolonging unsafe pregnancies.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prior spontaneous preterm birth, short cervix, multiple gestation, infection, smoking, uterine anomalies
Cervical surgery or prior painless second-trimester loss suggests cervical insufficiency

rows.label: Clues
items: Pelvic pressure, backache, increased discharge, contractions; assess membrane rupture and bleeding
Fever, uterine tenderness, fetal tachycardia → intraamniotic infection; maternal/fetal instability changes delivery timing

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Premature inflammatory/uterine activation versus mechanically weak cervix with painless dilation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Sterile speculum examination** for pooling and cervix; ultrasound dates pregnancy and assesses presentation
Transvaginal cervical length; selected symptomatic cases: negative fetal fibronectin predicts low imminent birth risk
Collect GBS culture, urine studies; exclude previa before digital examination with bleeding

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Birth within 7 days, **24–33 6/7 weeks** → betamethasone; selected untreated 34–36 6/7-week pregnancies also eligible
★ Delivery expected <32 weeks → **magnesium sulfate** for neuroprotection, not primary tocolysis
Tocolysis: 48 hours for steroids/transfer; no maintenance; late-preterm steroids avoided with pregestational diabetes
★ **No tocolysis** with infection, significant abruption, severe preeclampsia, or fetal compromise; proceed toward delivery
Intrapartum penicillin for positive/unknown GBS; no routine antibiotics for intact membranes without infection

rows.label: Complications
items: Neonatal RDS, IVH, NEC, sepsis, cerebral palsy; magnesium toxicity → hyporeflexia, respiratory depression

rows.label: Prevention
items: Singleton short cervix ≤20 mm before 24 weeks → vaginal progesterone; consider at 21–25 mm
Cervical insufficiency/prior qualifying loss → cerclage; prior preterm birth + cervix <25 mm before 24 weeks
17-hydroxyprogesterone caproate withdrawn 2023; progesterone without short cervix not routinely recommended
Older exam questions may expect 17-hydroxyprogesterone from 16–20 weeks after prior spontaneous preterm birth

rows.label: Mimics
items: Braxton Hicks: no progressive dilation
Cervical insufficiency: painless dilation, minimal contractions
PPROM: membrane rupture precedes labor; distinct latency-antibiotic pathway

primary-immunodeficiencies.name: Primary immunodeficiencies
primary-immunodeficiencies.scope: Selective IgA deficiency, common variable immunodeficiency (CVID), X-linked agammaglobulinemia, severe combined immunodeficiency, hyper-IgE syndrome, Wiskott-Aldrich, chronic granulomatous disease
primary-immunodeficiencies.core: Recurrent, unusually severe, persistent, or opportunistic infections; organism pattern and age of onset localize the immune defect.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Consanguinity, affected relatives, male relatives dying in infancy; absent family history does not exclude disease

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Failure to thrive, chronic diarrhea, persistent thrush, or infections across multiple organ systems
Deep abscesses suggest phagocyte dysfunction; recurrent encapsulated bacteria suggest impaired antibody function

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Selective IgA deficiency: impaired mucosal defense; respiratory infections, giardiasis, atopy, or no symptoms
Antibody disorders impair opsonization; T-cell defects permit viral, fungal, and protozoal opportunists
DiGeorge: 3rd/4th **pharyngeal pouch** failure → absent thymus, hypocalcemia, conotruncal defects, T-cell infections
ADA deficiency: autosomal recessive SCID; toxic deoxyadenosine destroys T and B cells

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Start **CBC with differential, quantitative immunoglobulins**, HIV testing; assess vaccine antibody responses
Lymphocyte subsets distinguish B-cell and T-cell deficiencies; abnormal results → genetic confirmation
IgA deficiency: isolated IgA <7 mg/dL after age 4 years; normal IgG and IgM
★ Newborn **TREC screen** detects impaired T-cell production before symptomatic SCID

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Profound combined immune failure → isolation, irradiated CMV-negative blood products, urgent **transplant evaluation**
Acute infections: organism-directed antimicrobials; immunoglobulin replacement not useful for isolated IgA deficiency

rows.label: Complications
items: Bronchiectasis, chronic enteropathy, autoimmune disease; CVID additionally increases lymphoma risk
Anti-IgA antibodies can cause anaphylaxis to blood products

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Avoid **live vaccines** in major T-cell defects; immunize household contacts with safe vaccine choices
IgA-related transfusion reactions → washed cellular products or IgA-deficient plasma
CGD: TMP-SMX + itraconazole prophylaxis; genetic counseling for inherited defects

rows.label: Mimics
items: Vertical HIV: bacterial infections + zoster, nodes, maternal opportunistic infection; low CD4, positive virologic testing
Secondary hypogammaglobulinemia: nephrotic protein loss, B-cell malignancy, or rituximab exposure

table.title: Defect fingerprints
rows: Adolescent/adult; low IgG, poor vaccine response
Boy after 6 months; absent tonsils/B cells
Infant; absent thymic shadow, profound lymphopenia
Cold abscesses, eczema, retained teeth, pneumatoceles

primary-immunodeficiencies.evidence: Not checked online; established clinical immunology teaching.

prostate-carcinoma.name: Prostate carcinoma
prostate-carcinoma.scope: Adenocarcinoma, Gleason score, osteoblastic bone metastases, androgen deprivation therapy, radical prostatectomy, radiation
prostate-carcinoma.core: Older man with an abnormal PSA or hard prostatic nodule; risk stratification separates indolent localized disease from potentially lethal systemic cancer.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Increasing age, Black ancestry, first-degree family history, BRCA2/Lynch-associated predisposition

rows.label: Clues
items: Often asymptomatic; urinary obstruction or hematuria usually later; peripheral-zone tumors may spare early urinary flow
★ Persistent back/bone pain, **osteoblastic lesions**, elevated alkaline phosphatase → metastatic disease
New weakness, saddle anesthesia, urinary retention → possible spinal cord/cauda equina compression

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Gland-forming adenocarcinoma; androgen-receptor signaling promotes growth; spread to pelvic nodes and axial skeleton

rows.label: Dx
items: Newly elevated PSA without urgent findings → repeat after transient causes resolve; PSA not cancer-specific
★ **Prostate MRI → targeted plus systematic core biopsy** when suspicion warrants; histology confirms
Negative MRI plus high clinical risk → systematic biopsy; no single PSA threshold excludes cancer
★ **Gleason = primary + secondary patterns**; 4+3 worse than 3+4; Grade Group 1–5
Stage using PSA, biopsy grade, clinical extent; high-risk/metastatic suspicion → PSMA PET/CT or conventional bone/CT imaging

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Metastatic hormone-sensitive disease → **ADT + abiraterone/prednisone or enzalutamide**
Selected fit metastatic cases → add docetaxel; castration-resistant progression → continue ADT, add other agents
GnRH agonist leuprolide → initial flare; short antiandrogen cover; antagonist degarelix avoids flare
Suspected cord compression → **dexamethasone + urgent spinal MRI**, then radiation/surgical decompression

rows.label: Complications
items: Surgery: urinary incontinence, erectile dysfunction; radiation: proctitis, cystitis, erectile dysfunction
ADT: hot flashes, sexual dysfunction, osteoporosis, metabolic/cardiovascular toxicity; assess fracture risk

rows.label: Prevention
items: No proven primary prevention; PSA screening requires benefit/overdiagnosis discussion
USPSTF: shared decision age **55–69**; no routine screening ≥70; AUA offers earlier risk-based discussion

rows.label: Mimics
items: BPH: smooth symmetric enlargement, transition zone; lower urinary symptoms predominate
Prostatitis: tender/boggy gland, dysuria, fever; PSA may transiently rise

rh-alloimmunization.name: Rh alloimmunization
rh-alloimmunization.scope: Rh(D) and other red cell alloimmunization (Kell, Duffy), anti-D immune globulin prophylaxis, indirect Coombs titer monitoring, fetomaternal hemorrhage (Kleihauer-Betke), middle cerebral artery Doppler for fetal anemia
rh-alloimmunization.core: Maternal IgG against fetal red-cell antigens crosses the placenta, causing fetal anemia, hydrops, and neonatal hemolysis.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Antigen-negative mother/positive fetus; prior pregnancy, transfusion, bleeding, trauma, invasive procedures
Anti-D, anti-Kell, and anti-Duffy clinically significant; ABO incompatibility usually milder

rows.label: Clues
items: Often asymptomatic mother; fetal ascites, skin edema, placentomegaly, cardiomegaly
Neonate: early jaundice, pallor, reticulocytosis, **positive direct Coombs**; severe disease → cardiovascular collapse

rows.label: Pathophys
items: First exposure sensitizes; subsequent antigen exposure produces an anamnestic response
Kell antibodies additionally suppress erythropoiesis; low titers can still cause severe disease

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ First prenatal visit: ABO/Rh type + **indirect Coombs**; repeat before routine antenatal prophylaxis
Antibody → **paternal antigen typing**; negative (certain paternity) → no fetal risk; else fetal typing, titers
★ Critical titer, often **1:16**, or previously affected pregnancy → middle cerebral artery Doppler
MCA peak systolic velocity >1.5 MoM → fetal blood sampling; Kell warrants specialist surveillance
Kleihauer-Betke quantifies hemorrhage for dosing: **300 µg covers 30 mL fetal whole blood**

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Severe preterm fetal anemia → **intrauterine transfusion**; near term → delivery
Neonatal hyperbilirubinemia → phototherapy; severe hemolysis → exchange transfusion

rows.label: Complications
items: High-output heart failure, stillbirth, bilirubin encephalopathy, delayed neonatal anemia

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Unsensitized Rh-negative mother: **anti-D immune globulin** at 28 weeks and within 72 hours postpartum
Sensitizing event → dose now; lasts ~12 weeks, repeat at 28; postpartum only if Rh-positive/unknown infant
★ Established anti-D sensitization → prophylaxis ineffective; no equivalent prophylaxis for Kell/Duffy
ACOG 2024: routine Rh testing/prophylaxis may be forgone for abortion/loss before 12 weeks

rows.label: Mimics
items: Parvovirus: nonimmune hydrops with negative maternal antibody screen
ABO hemolysis: may affect first pregnancy; fetal hydrops uncommon

rh-alloimmunization.evidence: Prophylaxis checked 2026-10-30: [ACOG Rh guidance](https://www.acog.org/womens-health/faqs/the-rh-factor-how-it-can-affect-your-pregnancy), [2024 update](https://doi.org/10.1097/AOG.0000000000005733); remaining content established teaching.

schizophrenia-spectrum-disorders.name: Schizophrenia spectrum disorders
schizophrenia-spectrum-disorders.scope: Brief psychotic disorder, schizophreniform disorder, schizophrenia, schizoaffective disorder, mesolimbic dopamine
schizophrenia-spectrum-disorders.core: Psychosis with impaired reality testing: distinguish schizophrenia-spectrum disorders by duration, functional decline, and the relationship between mood episodes and psychosis.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Family history, neurodevelopmental vulnerability; adolescent cannabis exposure increases risk
Typical onset late adolescence/early adulthood; exclude stimulant, hallucinogen, medication, and neurologic causes

rows.label: Clues
items: Delusions, hallucinations, disorganized speech/behavior; negative symptoms: avolition, alogia, flat affect
★ At least **two core symptoms**, including delusions, hallucinations, or disorganized speech, for active-phase diagnosis
Suicidality, dangerous commands or inability to eat → urgent safety assessment

rows.label: Pathophys
items: ★ **↑Mesolimbic dopamine** → positive symptoms; mesocortical → negative symptoms, early working-memory deficits
D2 blockade reduces psychosis but nigrostriatal/tuberoinfundibular effects cause EPS and hyperprolactinemia
Structural correlate: **enlarged lateral and third ventricles**, reduced cortical volume

rows.label: Dx
items: Clinical history, collateral information, mental status; assess mood timeline and substance exposure
First episode → CBC/CMP, TSH, toxicology; HIV/syphilis or neuroimaging for relevant risks/atypical neurologic findings
★ **Schizoaffective**: ≥2 weeks psychosis without mood episode; mood episodes occupy most illness duration

rows.label: Tx
items: Safety crisis → hospitalization; acute agitation → de-escalation, then medication if needed
★ **Risperidone, aripiprazole or olanzapine** + coordinated specialty care, family education, CBT, supported employment
Schizoaffective depressive/bipolar subtype → add antidepressant or mood stabilizer according to mood syndrome
★ Failure of two adequate antipsychotic trials or persistent substantial suicide risk → **clozapine**
Adherence difficulty → long-acting injectable (haloperidol decanoate); catatonia → lorazepam, then ECT if refractory

rows.label: Complications
items: Suicide, homelessness, substance use, cardiometabolic disease; antipsychotics → metabolic syndrome, tardive dyskinesia, NMS
Clozapine → neutropenia, myocarditis, severe constipation; monitor ANC and symptoms

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid cannabis/stimulants; maintenance medication, relapse planning reduce recurrence
Monitor weight, BP, glucose, lipids; address tobacco use and cardiovascular risk
**High expressed emotion** (family criticism, hostility) → relapse; family therapy reduces recurrence

rows.label: Mimics
items: Mood disorder with psychosis: psychosis occurs exclusively during mood episodes
Delirium: fluctuating attention/awareness and acute medical cause
Delusional disorder: ≥1 month delusions with otherwise relatively preserved function, limited other psychotic symptoms
Substance/medication-induced psychosis: recent stimulants (mydriasis, tremor) or corticosteroids, intact orientation

secondary-hypertension.name: Secondary hypertension
secondary-hypertension.scope: Renal artery stenosis, primary hyperaldosteronism, pheochromocytoma, Cushing syndrome, coarctation of aorta, diagnostic workup
secondary-hypertension.core: Abrupt, unusually young, severe, or resistant hypertension suggests a treatable secondary driver.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Renal stenosis: older smoker → atherosclerotic **lipid plaque**; young/middle-aged woman → **fibromuscular dysplasia** (medial hyperplasia, renal + carotid)
Renal disease, adrenal tumors, sleep apnea
NSAIDs, oral contraceptives, stimulants, glucocorticoids, licorice; medication nonadherence can mimic resistance

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Hypokalemia + metabolic alkalosis** → aldosterone excess, primary or renovascular; normal K does not exclude it
**Abdominal bruit**, diffuse atherosclerosis, late abrupt worsening, small unilateral kidney → renal artery stenosis
Flash pulmonary edema or creatinine rise >30% after ACE inhibitor/ARB → renovascular disease
**Episodic headache, sweating, palpitations** → pheochromocytoma; cushingoid appearance, upper-body hypertension guide testing

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Renal hypoperfusion → juxtaglomerular **renin** → RAAS; ACE inhibitor removes efferent constriction → ↓renal flow, ↓GFR across stenosis
Autonomous aldosterone → distal sodium absorption, potassium loss, low renin; pressure natriuresis escape prevents edema
Adrenal medullary catecholamine or cortisol excess, aortic obstruction, or nocturnal hypoxia increases vascular pressure

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Confirm **home/ambulatory BP**, adherence, cuff technique; BMP, urinalysis, creatinine, TSH
Sleep-apnea symptoms → polysomnography; abnormal urinary sediment → renal ultrasound and kidney evaluation
★ Biochemical testing precedes adrenal imaging; correct hypokalemia and account for interfering medications
Endocrine Society 2025: suggest **aldosterone screening for all hypertension**, conditional on resources

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Primary aldosteronism: unilateral → **adrenalectomy**; bilateral → spironolactone/eplerenone
Renovascular atherosclerosis → medical risk reduction; revascularize selected recurrent pulmonary edema or refractory disease
Fibromuscular dysplasia → angioplasty; critical bilateral renal stenosis → avoid ACE inhibitor/ARB
★ Pheochromocytoma: **alpha blockade before beta blockade**, volume expansion, then surgery
Treat cortisol source, repair significant coarctation, use CPAP for OSA; stop contributing drugs

rows.label: Complications
items: Stroke, MI, heart failure, CKD, retinopathy
Unopposed alpha stimulation after beta blockade can cause catecholamine crisis

rows.label: Prevention
items: Monitor renal function/K after RAAS blockers or mineralocorticoid antagonists
Genetic evaluation/family screening for suspected hereditary pheochromocytoma or congenital aortic disease

rows.label: Mimics
items: White-coat hypertension: normal out-of-office readings
Essential hypertension: gradual course without specific endocrine/renal clues

table.title: Targeted workup
rows: Selective suppression test; CT/adrenal venous sampling
Plasma free or urine fractionated metanephrines

secondary-hypertension.evidence: Aldosterone screening checked 2026-10-30: [Endocrine Society 2025](https://www.endocrine.org/clinical-practice-guidelines/primary-aldosteronism-2); other causes: established teaching.

septic-arthritis.name: Septic arthritis
septic-arthritis.scope: Nongonococcal, gonococcal, prosthetic joint infection, IV drug use, empiric coverage (vancomycin + cefepime), contiguous osteomyelitis
septic-arthritis.core: Acutely painful swollen joint with restricted passive motion → urgent aspiration and drainage; delayed treatment rapidly destroys cartilage.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prosthesis, recent surgery/injection, rheumatoid arthritis, immunosuppression, diabetes, bacteremia
IV drug use → S aureus and gram-negative risk, including Pseudomonas
Young sexually active adults → disseminated gonorrhea; adjacent ulcers/osteomyelitis → contiguous spread
RA joint with new febrile monoarthritis → infection until aspirated, not flare

rows.label: Clues
items: Usually acute monoarthritis, often knee; fever may be absent, especially in older/immunocompromised adults
★ **Severe pain with both active and passive motion**; inability to bear weight; child's hip held flexed, abducted, externally rotated
Gonococcal dissemination: migratory polyarthralgia, tenosynovitis, sparse pustules; may progress to purulent monoarthritis
Prosthetic infection: persistent pain, loosening, wound drainage or sinus tract, sometimes minimal systemic illness

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Hematogenous seeding or direct inoculation → neutrophilic enzymes damage articular cartilage
Implant biofilm limits antibiotic eradication without surgical source control
★ **S aureus** most common, including RA-damaged joints: gram-positive cocci in clusters
Asplenia or recent pharyngitis → **streptococci**: gram-positive cocci in chains

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Arthrocentesis before antibiotics** when stable: cell count/differential, Gram stain, culture, crystals
Synovial WBC >50,000/µL, neutrophil predominance supports infection; lower counts or negative Gram stain never exclude
★ **Crystals do not exclude infection**; send cultures even when gout seems likely
Blood cultures; gonococcal: aspirate on **chocolate/Thayer-Martin agar** plus mucosal NAAT; MRI for suspected contiguous osteomyelitis
New warmth/effusion in OA joint → aspirate before any intra-articular steroid

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ After cultures → **IV vancomycin + cefepime or piperacillin-tazobactam** for severe disease, IV drug use, gram-negative risk
Stable low-risk adult: vancomycin ± ceftriaxone based on exposure; narrow to organism/susceptibility
Sepsis → immediate antibiotics without delaying for aspiration; large joints: arthroscopic washout; **hip → operative drainage**, not serial aspiration
Persistent symptoms → repeat drainage, seek abscess/osteomyelitis; mobilize after infection controlled

rows.label: Complications
items: Irreversible joint destruction, avascular necrosis, osteomyelitis, bacteremia, sepsis
Prolonged antibiotics → renal injury, line complications, C difficile; prolonged immobility → stiffness

rows.label: Prevention
items: Sterile procedures, treat skin infections, injection-harm reduction
Gonorrhea: treat partners, screen other STIs, abstain until treatment completed and partners treated

rows.label: Mimics
items: Crystal arthritis: polarized crystals; infection still possible concurrently
Bursitis: localized periarticular swelling, passive joint motion relatively preserved
Reactive arthritis: sterile inflammatory arthritis after GI/GU infection
Transient synovitis (child): afebrile, bears weight, ESR <40, WBC <12,000

table.title: Special treatment branches
rows: Debridement, implant retention, prolonged pathogen-directed antibiotics

sexual-dysfunction.name: Sexual dysfunction
sexual-dysfunction.scope: Female orgasmic disorder, female sexual interest/arousal disorder, genito-pelvic pain/penetration disorder, premature ejaculation, SSRI-induced sexual dysfunction
sexual-dysfunction.core: Persistent, distressing impairment of desire, arousal, orgasm, ejaculation, or penetration; classify the affected phase before choosing treatment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Depression, anxiety, relationship conflict, sexual trauma, menopause
Diabetes, neurologic disease, pelvic surgery; SSRIs, antipsychotics, opioids

rows.label: Clues
items: Interest/arousal: ↓interest, fantasies, initiation, pleasure, cue response, genital sensations; assess adequate stimulation
★ Penetration pain/fear, pelvic-floor spasm blocking tampon/speculum → genito-pelvic pain/penetration disorder (**vaginismus**)
Low lubrication, vaginal dryness, postcoital spotting → assess estrogen deficiency

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Serotonergic inhibition of sexual response; hypoestrogenism → mucosal atrophy
Performance anxiety and pain avoidance reinforce dysfunction
Bilateral oophorectomy → ↓**ovarian androgens** → low libido despite estrogen replacement, normal vaginal mucosa

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Symptoms usually ≥6 months + personal distress; frequency criteria depend on disorder
Private sexual/relationship history; review drugs, coercion, mood, and medical causes
Pelvic examination for pain; TSH, prolactin, glucose only when history suggests abnormality
Low desire without distress → normal variation; inadequate stimulation alone ≠ orgasmic disorder

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Education, couples/sex counseling, CBT; treat underlying disease and relationship contributors
Penetration disorder → pelvic-floor physical treatment, graded dilators; vaginal estrogen for menopausal atrophy
★ SSRI-induced: reduce dose if feasible, switch to or augment with **bupropion**
Acquired generalized HSDD: flibanserin in women <65, including postmenopause; separate from alcohol
Flibanserin: avoid hepatic impairment and moderate/strong CYP3A4 inhibitors; not for drug-induced low desire

rows.label: Complications
items: Avoidance, relationship strain, reduced quality of life
Flibanserin: syncope; topical penile anesthetics: partner numbness

rows.label: Mimics
items: Vulvodynia: localized provoked vestibular tenderness
Major depression: pervasive anhedonia beyond sexual situations
Normal aging: slower response without clinically significant distress

sexual-dysfunction.evidence: FDA label checked 2026-10-30: [flibanserin, 2025](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2025/022526s013lbl.pdf); other content established teaching.

shock.name: Shock
shock.scope: Hypovolemic, cardiogenic, distributive (septic, anaphylactic, neurogenic), obstructive, fluid resuscitation, vasopressors
shock.core: Circulatory failure causing tissue hypoperfusion; normal blood pressure does not exclude early shock.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Hemorrhage, GI losses, MI, infection, allergen exposure, spinal injury, thromboembolism
Recent surgery, immunosuppression, indwelling devices increase occult infection risk
Procedure bleeding: thoracentesis → intercostal artery, hemothorax; splenectomy → hemoperitoneum, left shoulder pain

rows.label: Clues
items: Tachycardia, altered mentation, oliguria, cool mottled skin; distributive forms may initially feel warm
★ **Anaphylaxis**: rapid airway swelling, wheezing, hypotension; skin findings may be absent
Neurogenic: **lost sympathetic tone** → hypotension, bradycardia or no tachycardia, warm skin after spinal cord injury

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Oxygen delivery falls below demand → anaerobic metabolism, lactate accumulation
Distributive vasodilation → relative hypovolemia despite normal total body fluid
Warm sepsis: high output, **high mixed venous O2**; pump failure: low contractility, congestion; hypovolemia: low preload

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Bedside ultrasound**: cardiac function, pericardial fluid, RV dilation, lung sliding, volume assessment
**Serial lactate**: hypoperfusion, best predicts course and mortality; trend with capillary refill, urine output
Septic shock: vasopressors for MAP ≥65 plus lactate >2 despite volume resuscitation
CBC, chemistry, ECG, troponin; cultures if infection suspected

rows.label: Tx
items: Airway, IV access; **isotonic crystalloid** (balanced, 0.9% saline) before imaging; restrict with pulmonary congestion
★ Hemorrhage → **control bleeding + blood products** (emergency O-negative); crystalloid as bridge; no vasopressors
★ Septic shock → antibiotics within 1 hour, drainage/debridement; crystalloid 30 mL/kg within 3 hours
★ Persistent septic hypotension → **norepinephrine**, MAP ≥65; add vasopressin, then epinephrine; refractory → hydrocortisone
Pulmonary edema after fluids → stop boluses, **inotrope**; children: epinephrine preferred, older exams may expect dopamine

rows.label: Complications
items: AKI, ischemic hepatitis, DIC, ARDS, bowel ischemia, multiorgan failure
Excess fluids → edema; vasopressors → digital/mesenteric ischemia

rows.label: Prevention
items: Early infection treatment, catheter hygiene, VTE prophylaxis, hemorrhage control
After anaphylaxis: trigger avoidance, epinephrine autoinjector, allergy referral

rows.label: Mimics
items: Vasovagal syncope: transient bradycardia, rapid recovery supine
Hypoglycemia: low bedside glucose, improvement with dextrose
Isolated head injury: hypertension + bradycardia (Cushing); trauma hypotension + tachycardia → assume hemorrhage

table.title: Hemodynamics and cause-directed rescue
rows: Decompress pneumothorax; drain tamponade; reperfuse PE

sickle-cell-disease.name: Sickle cell disease
sickle-cell-disease.scope: Vaso-occlusive pain crisis, acute chest syndrome, splenic sequestration, aplastic crisis, stroke, sickle cell trait, hemoglobin electrophoresis
sickle-cell-disease.core: HbS polymerization causes chronic hemolysis and episodic vascular occlusion; fever, hypoxemia and focal neurologic deficits require urgent escalation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Autosomal recessive β-globin disease; dehydration, hypoxemia, cold and infection trigger sickling
Functional asplenia → encapsulated infection from early childhood; **S. pneumoniae** leads pneumonia and fulminant sepsis

rows.label: Clues
items: Baseline anemia, reticulocytosis, jaundice; childhood dactylitis or recurrent severe bone pain
Acute chest syndrome: **new pulmonary infiltrate** plus fever, respiratory symptoms or hypoxemia
Sequestration: sudden splenomegaly, falling hemoglobin, shock; aplasia: **low reticulocyte count**, often parvovirus

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Deoxygenated hemoglobin polymerizes → rigid erythrocytes, endothelial injury, ischemia and shortened RBC survival
Acute chest trigger: **infection** most common; in situ thrombosis and fat embolism less often
Severe anemia → low viscosity, vasodilation, ↓afterload → **↑cardiac output** preserves oxygen delivery

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Hemoglobin electrophoresis/HPLC confirms genotype; newborn screen detects disease before symptoms
Crisis → CBC, reticulocytes, bilirubin; fever → blood cultures; respiratory symptoms → chest radiograph
New focal deficit → emergency brain imaging, without delaying transfusion preparation
Distinguish osteomyelitis from infarction using cultures and MRI when focal fever/pain persists

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Pain crisis → prompt **IV opioid**, morphine (AKI: lower dose or hydromorphone); no meperidine; NSAID only if kidneys normal
Pain crisis support: euvolemic hydration; oxygen only for hypoxemia; no routine transfusion
★ Acute chest → oxygen, **ceftriaxone + azithromycin**, incentive spirometry; transfuse for significant anemia
Severe acute chest, stroke → **urgent exchange transfusion**; sequestration (cautious) or aplasia → simple transfusion
Fever → immediate **IV ceftriaxone/cefotaxime**, despite daily penicillin prophylaxis

rows.label: Complications
items: Stroke, avascular necrosis, priapism, pigment gallstones, nephropathy, retinopathy
Repeated transfusions → alloimmunization and iron overload; delayed hyperhemolysis can worsen anemia
Chronic hemolysis → ↑folate demand → **folate deficiency**, macrocytosis

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Hydroxyurea** raises HbF, reduces crises; monitor CBC
Penicillin prophylaxis through age 5 in HbSS; pneumococcal, meningococcal, Hib and influenza vaccines
Annual transcranial Doppler ages 2–16 in HbSS/HbSβ0; abnormal → chronic transfusion program

rows.label: Mimics
items: Osteomyelitis: persistent localized pain, fever; Salmonella or S. aureus
Iron deficiency: low ferritin, no hemolytic pattern

sjogren-syndrome.name: Sjogren syndrome
sjogren-syndrome.scope: Primary Sjogren syndrome, keratoconjunctivitis sicca, xerostomia, anti-Ro/SSA, anti-La/SSB, B-cell lymphoma risk
sjogren-syndrome.core: Autoimmune exocrine gland dysfunction causing persistent dry eyes and dry mouth, often in a middle-aged woman with fatigue or inflammatory arthralgia.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Female sex; primary disease alone or secondary association with rheumatoid arthritis/SLE
Autoimmune thyroid disease or another autoimmune condition increases suspicion

rows.label: Clues
items: Gritty/burning eyes, difficulty swallowing dry food, frequent sipping, recurrent dental caries, oral candidiasis
★ **Bilateral parotid enlargement**; absent salivary pooling, fissured tongue; vaginal dryness possible
Systemic disease: palpable purpura, peripheral neuropathy, interstitial lung disease, tubulointerstitial nephritis
Distal renal tubular acidosis → non-anion-gap acidosis, hypokalemia, inappropriately alkaline urine

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Lymphocytic lacrimal/salivary gland infiltration and B-cell hyperactivity → gland destruction and autoantibodies

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Anti-Ro/SSA** most useful antibody; anti-La/SSB supportive; ANA/RF commonly positive
★ **Schirmer ≤5 mm/5 minutes** or ocular surface staining documents aqueous tear deficiency
Unstimulated salivary flow ≤0.1 mL/min; uncertain/seronegative disease → minor labial salivary gland biopsy
Biopsy: focal lymphocytic sialadenitis; assess CBC, creatinine, urinalysis, electrolytes for systemic involvement

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Artificial tears**; severe ocular inflammation → ophthalmic cyclosporine/lifitegrast under ophthalmology
Frequent water, sugar-free gum, saliva substitutes; **pilocarpine or cevimeline** for residual gland function
Muscarinic agonists: sweating, bronchospasm; avoid uncontrolled asthma or narrow-angle glaucoma
Inflammatory arthritis → hydroxychloroquine; severe organ disease → glucocorticoids ± organ-directed immunosuppression
Oral candidiasis → nystatin or fluconazole; do not use systemic steroids for isolated sicca

rows.label: Complications
items: Corneal abrasion/ulceration, dental loss; renal electrolyte disturbances, pulmonary disease
★ **B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma**, especially MALT; persistent unilateral gland enlargement, nodes or B symptoms → biopsy

rows.label: Prevention
items: Fluoride toothpaste, regular dental visits, oral hygiene; avoid tobacco and anticholinergic medications
Ophthalmology follow-up; assess new gland masses, purpura or constitutional symptoms promptly

rows.label: Mimics
items: Medication-induced sicca: anticholinergic/antihistamine exposure without autoimmune gland findings
Hepatitis C/HIV: infectious testing identifies alternative sicca syndrome
IgG4-related disease: prominent gland swelling, characteristic storiform fibrosis and IgG4-positive plasma cells

sjogren-syndrome.evidence: Management checked 2026-10-30: [BSR Sjögren guideline, 2024](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12013823/); diagnostic criteria: established rheumatology teaching.

solid-organ-transplantation.name: Solid organ transplantation
solid-organ-transplantation.scope: Hyperacute rejection, acute allograft rejection, chronic allograft rejection, immunosuppressive regimens
solid-organ-transplantation.core: Allograft dysfunction requires urgent distinction among rejection, infection, obstruction/vascular failure, and immunosuppressant toxicity; biopsy usually establishes the rejection mechanism.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: HLA mismatch; sensitization after transplant, transfusion or pregnancy → preformed donor-specific antibodies
Missed immunosuppression, underdosing, drug interactions; rejection can occur late after medication withdrawal

rows.label: Clues
items: Kidney: ↑creatinine; liver: ↑bilirubin/enzymes; heart: ventricular dysfunction; lung: ↓spirometry
Fever, graft tenderness or malaise possible; rejection may be asymptomatic before laboratory abnormalities

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Allorecognition targets donor tissue; immunosuppression balances graft protection against infection and malignancy

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Graft ultrasound/Doppler** when relevant → exclude obstruction, thrombosis or vascular compromise
Medication adherence/troughs, cultures and organ-specific viral testing; donor-specific antibodies assess humoral injury
★ **Allograft biopsy** distinguishes rejection from drug toxicity/infection; C4d may support antibody-mediated injury

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Common kidney maintenance: **tacrolimus + mycophenolate ± prednisone**; regimen varies by organ and risk
Induction in selected recipients → basiliximab or antithymocyte globulin
Steroid-resistant cellular rejection → antithymocyte globulin; coordinate all treatment with transplant team
Never reflexively escalate immunosuppression for unexplained fever before evaluating infection

rows.label: Complications
items: Calcineurin inhibitors → nephrotoxicity, hypertension, neurotoxicity; tacrolimus → diabetes
Mycophenolate → cytopenias, diarrhea, teratogenicity; sirolimus → poor wound healing, hyperlipidemia
Glucocorticoids → diabetes/osteoporosis; immunosuppression → opportunistic infection, skin cancer, EBV-related PTLD

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **ABO compatibility, HLA assessment, crossmatch** before transplant; lifelong adherence and trough monitoring
TMP-SMX prophylaxis for Pneumocystis; valganciclovir or preemptive monitoring for CMV according to risk
Vaccinate before transplant; avoid live vaccines during immunosuppression; sun protection and skin checks

rows.label: Mimics
items: Calcineurin toxicity: excessive exposure, no graft tenderness/enlargement; compatible biopsy, no alloimmune infiltrates
BK nephropathy: kidney transplant, viral PCR and viral inclusions on biopsy
Mechanical graft failure: obstruction/thrombosis demonstrated by imaging

table.title: Rejection patterns
rows: T-cell infiltrates; liver: portal eosinophils, endotheliitis

somatic-symptom-disorders.name: Somatic symptom disorders
somatic-symptom-disorders.scope: Somatic symptom disorder, illness anxiety disorder, conversion disorder, factitious disorder, malingering, regular scheduled visits, validating suffering
somatic-symptom-disorders.core: Distressing symptoms or health fears require a positive psychiatric formulation, validation, and proportionate medical evaluation; intent separates factitious behavior from functional symptoms.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Trauma, anxiety/depression, chronic illness, major stress; medical and psychiatric disorders can coexist

rows.label: Clues
items: Persistent reassurance seeking, repeated testing, high health-related distress, impaired function
Assess suicidality, abuse, substance use, and medication-related symptoms; avoid assumptions based on demographics
Functional blindness: intact **pupillary reflex, threat blink, optokinetic nystagmus**
Extreme fever + normal pulse/labs → suspect falsification; **supervised rectal temperature** before antibiotics

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Attention, threat appraisal, and learned responses amplify suffering; symptoms do not require conscious production
External reward differs from internal sick-role motivation; neither can be inferred from one inconsistency

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Somatic symptom disorder does not require medically unexplained symptoms**; excessive response is decisive
Illness anxiety requires ≥6 months preoccupation; somatic symptom persistence typically >6 months
★ Functional neurologic: **incompatible signs**: Hoover, give-way weakness, midline sensory split, forehead vibration discrepancy
Nonepileptic seizures: captured spell without **video-EEG** epileptiform change; often acute stressor
New objective abnormalities still warrant targeted medical evaluation; avoid diagnosing solely by exhaustive exclusion

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **One clinician, scheduled visits**, focused examinations; validate suffering without endorsing unproven disease
CBT, functional rehabilitation, treat comorbid anxiety/depression
Functional deficits → empathic explanation, expected recovery; nonepileptic seizures → **CBT**, no antiseizure drugs
★ Functional deficit or negative workups → **psychiatric assessment**, no more procedures; **new red flags → reassess**
Factitious: team approach, factual records, no confrontation, evaluate psychiatric comorbidity; protect dependents from induced illness

rows.label: Complications
items: Iatrogenic injury, unnecessary surgery, opioid exposure, disability, fragmented care
Factitious disorder imposed on another → serious abuse risk requiring safeguarding action

rows.label: Mimics
items: Occult medical disease: evolving objective findings or coherent physiologic abnormalities
Delusional disorder: fixed somatic belief despite evidence, without flexible doubt

table.title: Distinguishing patterns
rows: Motor/sensory symptoms incompatible with neurologic disease
Intentional deception; no obvious external reward
Intentional symptoms, external gain; no treatment/invasive testing

somatic-symptom-disorders.evidence: Not checked online; established DSM-5-TR teaching.

spinal-cord-compression.name: Spinal cord compression
spinal-cord-compression.scope: Neoplastic spinal cord compression (epidural metastases, dexamethasone, emergent MRI), spinal epidural abscess (fever, IV drug use, empiric antibiotics), cauda equina syndrome, surgical decompression
spinal-cord-compression.core: Back pain with new weakness, sensory changes or sphincter dysfunction requires urgent MRI to identify reversible neural compression.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Known breast, prostate, lung, renal cancer or myeloma → epidural metastases
IV drug use, bacteremia, diabetes, spinal procedure or immunosuppression → epidural abscess
Large lumbar disc herniation, trauma or spinal stenosis → cauda equina compression
Anticoagulation + epidural catheter placement/removal → **spinal epidural hematoma**: acute paraplegia, incontinence

rows.label: Clues
items: Progressive nocturnal pain, pain with cough/strain, radicular symptoms; deficits may be initially subtle
Cord lesion: sensory level, spastic weakness, hyperreflexia below lesion after acute phase
★ Cauda equina: **saddle anesthesia, urinary retention**, reduced anal tone, asymmetric flaccid leg weakness
Epidural abscess: fever/back pain ± deficit; classic triad often incomplete

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Epidural tumor, infection or disc material compresses neural tissue and impairs blood supply
Longstanding compression produces irreversible ischemic injury; bladder dysfunction signals advanced disease

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Urgent contrast MRI** of suspected region; whole spine for suspected metastatic compression
Postvoid residual supports retention assessment but normal result does not exclude early cauda equina syndrome
Suspected abscess → blood cultures, CBC, ESR/CRP; image before LP
MRI unavailable/contraindicated → CT myelography; ordinary radiographs cannot exclude epidural pathology

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Malignant compression with deficit → **dexamethasone immediately**, urgent neurosurgery/radiation consultation
Tumor → decompression/stabilization ± radiotherapy; choice depends on stability, neurologic function and prognosis
★ Epidural abscess → **vancomycin + cefepime**, cultures; urgent decompression for deficits or instability
Cauda equina syndrome → emergency spinal surgical assessment and **decompression**
Immobilize if instability suspected; bladder drainage and analgesia during definitive treatment

rows.label: Complications
items: Permanent paralysis, bowel/bladder dysfunction, sexual dysfunction, pressure injuries and VTE
Abscess → sepsis; steroids can worsen uncontrolled infection

rows.label: Prevention
items: Rapid assessment of cancer-associated new back pain; sterile procedures and prompt bacteremia treatment

rows.label: Mimics
items: Mechanical strain: normal neurologic exam, no sphincter symptoms
Transverse myelitis: intrinsic cord lesion without external compression
Peripheral neuropathy: distal symmetric findings without sensory level

spinal-cord-compression.evidence: Not checked online; established neurologic and oncologic emergency principles.

spondyloarthritis.name: Spondyloarthritis
spondyloarthritis.scope: Ankylosing spondylitis, psoriatic arthritis, reactive arthritis, enteropathic arthritis, HLA-B27, sacroiliitis
spondyloarthritis.core: Seronegative inflammatory arthritis characterized by axial pain, enthesitis, or asymmetric peripheral arthritis; identify associated skin, eye, bowel, and genitourinary disease.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Onset usually before age 45; family history and **HLA-B27** association, strongest in axial disease
Immune-mediated predisposition; preceding Chlamydia or enteric infection can trigger reactive arthritis

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Morning stiffness >30 minutes**, nocturnal back pain, improvement with exercise rather than rest
Alternating buttock pain, reduced spinal mobility/chest expansion; Achilles/plantar enthesitis, dactylitis
★ Painful photophobic red eye → **anterior uveitis**, urgent ophthalmology

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Inflammation at entheses and sacroiliac joints → erosions followed by new bone formation/ankylosis
TNF and IL-17 pathways drive disease; RF/anti-CCP usually absent

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Pelvic radiograph** for sacroiliitis; persistent suspicion with normal radiograph → **MRI sacroiliac joints**
ESR/CRP support activity but may be normal; HLA-B27 neither confirms nor excludes disease
Effusion → aspirate if infection/crystals possible; reactive arthritis → exposure-directed Chlamydia NAAT

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Exercise/physical therapy + NSAID**, e.g., naproxen; avoid prolonged immobilization
Persistent active axial disease → TNF inhibitor, e.g., adalimumab, or IL-17 inhibitor, e.g., secukinumab
Peripheral arthritis → methotrexate/sulfasalazine, ineffective for purely axial disease; avoid chronic systemic steroids
Active IBD/recurrent uveitis → monoclonal TNF inhibitor preferred; avoid IL-17 blockade in active IBD
Treat active Chlamydia and partners; antibiotics do not routinely resolve established postinfectious arthritis

rows.label: Complications
items: Spinal fusion, osteoporosis and unstable vertebral fracture after minor trauma
Aortic regurgitation/conduction disease in longstanding axial disease; biologics → serious infection/TB reactivation

rows.label: Prevention
items: Smoking cessation, posture and extension exercises; fall precautions when spine ankylosed
Before biologics: TB/HBV testing and vaccination; sexual barrier protection reduces Chlamydia-associated episodes

rows.label: Mimics
items: Mechanical back pain: worse with activity, improved with rest, minimal morning stiffness
Rheumatoid arthritis: symmetric small-joint synovitis, usually no sacroiliitis; anti-CCP often positive
DISH: older adults, flowing anterior ligament ossification, preserved sacroiliac joints

table.title: Phenotypes
rows: Psoriasis, nail pitting, DIP arthritis; pencil-in-cup
Postinfection oligoarthritis; urethritis, conjunctivitis may coexist
Crohn/UC; peripheral arthritis often tracks bowel activity

stable-ischemic-heart-disease.name: Stable ischemic heart disease
stable-ischemic-heart-disease.scope: Stable angina pectoris, exercise stress testing, stress echocardiography, antianginal pharmacotherapy, invasive coronary angiography indications
stable-ischemic-heart-disease.core: Predictable exertional chest pressure relieved by rest reflects myocardial oxygen supply–demand mismatch; new rest symptoms require acute coronary syndrome evaluation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Smoking, diabetes, hypertension, dyslipidemia, CKD, older age, family history of premature CAD
Anemia, tachycardia, and uncontrolled blood pressure can worsen ischemic symptoms

rows.label: Clues
items: Substernal squeezing, arm/jaw radiation; dyspnea or exertional indigestion may be anginal equivalents
Normal resting ECG does not exclude CAD; examination often normal between episodes
★ **Crescendo symptoms, prolonged pain, rest pain**, instability → ECG/troponins and ACS pathway

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Flow-limiting coronary atherosclerosis restricts supply when demand rises
Microvascular dysfunction can produce ischemia despite absence of obstructive epicardial disease

rows.label: Dx
items: Resting ECG, lipid profile, HbA1c, renal function; estimate clinical likelihood before choosing testing
★ Selected intermediate-risk suspected CAD → **CCTA or stress testing**, based on suitability
★ **Coronary angiography** for high-risk noninvasive findings, refractory limiting symptoms, or suspected high-risk anatomy
Stable on medical therapy, low-risk ischemia → no repeat testing or mandatory catheterization; respect informed refusal
Sedentary, risk factors, starting vigorous exercise: no routine stress test; older exam questions may expect exercise ECG

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Relief → **sublingual nitroglycerin**; avoid with recent PDE-5 inhibitor use or hypotension
★ Prevention → **aspirin + high-intensity statin**; manage BP/diabetes, lifestyle and exercise
Antianginal first-line: beta blocker or calcium-channel blocker; persistent symptoms → long-acting nitrate or ranolazine
Beta blockers improve outcomes for selected recent MI/reduced EF indications, not all stable CAD indefinitely
Refractory symptoms → revascularization; CABG improves survival in left-main/selected complex multivessel disease

rows.label: Complications
items: MI, heart failure, malignant arrhythmia, sudden death
Nitrates → headache/hypotension; combining beta blocker with verapamil/diltiazem can cause bradycardia/heart block

rows.label: Prevention
items: Smoking cessation, Mediterranean-style diet, habitual activity; cardiac rehabilitation when eligible
ACE inhibitor/ARB when hypertension, diabetes, CKD, or reduced EF; adherence and lipid follow-up
Drug-eluting stent → **aspirin + clopidogrel**, not anticoagulant; stable CAD 6 months; older exam questions may expect 12

rows.label: Mimics
items: GERD: meal/recumbency association, regurgitation
Aortic stenosis: exertional symptoms with systolic murmur
Costochondritis: reproducible focal chest-wall tenderness
Variant (Prinzmetal) vasospasm: rest/nocturnal pain, **transient ST elevation**, nitrate relief, normal angiography → calcium-channel blocker

table.title: Functional test selection
rows: Exercise stress echocardiography or perfusion imaging

stable-ischemic-heart-disease.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [ACC chronic coronary disease guideline summary (2023)](https://www.acc.org/latest-in-cardiology/ten-points-to-remember/2023/07/17/19/06/2023-guideline-for-chronic-coronary-disease-gl-ccd/).

stridor.name: Stridor
stridor.scope: Laryngomalacia (inspiratory, worse supine), tracheomalacia (expiratory), vocal cord dysfunction (paradoxical adduction), vascular ring (biphasic, dysphagia), flexible laryngoscopy
stridor.core: Harsh upper-airway noise: respiratory phase localizes obstruction; age, feeding difficulty, and episodic triggers identify the cause.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Congenital airway abnormalities in infancy; prematurity, prior intubation, tracheoesophageal fistula → tracheal weakness
Exercise, stress, irritants → inducible laryngeal obstruction; aortic arch anomalies → extrinsic compression

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Retractions, cyanosis, apnea, exhaustion, or poor air movement** → impending respiratory failure
Feeding-associated choking, recurrent pneumonia, or poor growth → clinically significant obstruction

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Inspiratory: extrathoracic collapse; expiratory: intrathoracic collapse; biphasic: fixed central obstruction

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Stable unexplained upper-airway noise → **awake flexible laryngoscopy**
Dynamic bronchoscopy assesses distal collapse; CT angiography/MR angiography delineates vascular compression
Normal examination between episodes does not exclude inducible obstruction; visualize during symptoms/exercise
Flow-volume loop: flattened inspiratory limb supports variable extrathoracic obstruction; not definitive alone

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Distress → oxygen, minimize agitation, **urgent controlled airway** with anesthesia/ENT
Mild congenital malacia → observation, feeding assessment, upright feeding while awake; spontaneous improvement with growth
★ Severe laryngeal collapse with apnea/poor growth → **supraglottoplasty**
Severe tracheal collapse → CPAP; refractory disease → airway surgery
Inducible obstruction → speech-guided breathing; symptomatic vascular ring → surgical division

rows.label: Complications
items: Hypoxemia, aspiration, recurrent respiratory infections, growth failure; severe obstruction → arrest
Misdiagnosed inducible obstruction → unnecessary bronchodilators, glucocorticoids, or intubations

rows.label: Prevention
items: Supine sleep on flat surface despite positional noise; no prone sleeping or wedges
Avoid smoke exposure; swallowing assessment and feeding modifications reduce aspiration

rows.label: Mimics
items: Croup: acute barky cough after URI; responds to dexamethasone
Foreign body: abrupt choking; rigid bronchoscopy despite normal radiograph
Epiglottitis: fever, drooling, tripod posture; avoid upsetting child or bedside throat examination

table.title: Chronic or episodic causes
rows: Expiratory; barking cough, worsens with exertion
Biphasic wheeze, dysphagia; steroid-unresponsive; neck extension relieves

study-designs.name: Study designs
study-designs.scope: Case-control, cohort, cross-sectional, RCT, control selection, bias, internal and external validity
study-designs.core: Study design determines how participants are selected, when exposure/outcome are measured, and which associations can be estimated without avoidable bias.

rows.label: Definition
items: Internal validity: credible within-study inference; external validity: applicability elsewhere
**Selection/ascertainment bias**: institutional or already-ill sample misrepresents target population
Subjective scoring by different raters → **interobserver variability**; standardize criteria

rows.label: Interpret
items: ★ **Randomization balances confounders on average**; concealed allocation prevents enrollment bias
Blinding reduces behavior/assessment bias; intention-to-treat retains original randomized groups
Loss to follow-up can bias estimates when related to exposure and outcome

rows.label: Use when
items: ★ Case-control controls → **same source population** that produced cases, independent of exposure
Prospective measurement improves temporality but does not eliminate confounding in observational research
Life table: poorest 1-year survival → steepest interval drop, not lowest cumulative point

rows.label: Compare
items: Confounding: third-variable distortion; randomize, restrict, match, stratify, or adjust
Effect modification: association differs across strata; report rather than remove it
Clinician-chosen treatment → **selection bias/confounding by indication**; randomization prevents it

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Case-control sampling cannot directly estimate incidence or risk** without additional population data
★ Cross-sectional data lack reliable **temporal sequence**; prevalent cases favor longer survivors
Random selection supports generalizability; random assignment supports causal inference

study-designs.evidence: Established epidemiologic definitions; no clinical guideline involved.

substance-use-disorders.name: Substance use disorders
substance-use-disorders.scope: Diagnostic criteria (mild, moderate, severe), cocaine use disorder, amphetamine use disorder, cannabis use disorder, motivational interviewing, cognitive behavioral therapy, 12-step programs
substance-use-disorders.core: A problematic pattern causing impaired control, risky use, social impairment or physiologic adaptation defines substance use disorder; severity follows criterion count.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Family history, trauma, psychiatric comorbidity, early exposure, unstable housing and peer availability
Persistent psychosocial stress and limited treatment access worsen trajectory

rows.label: Clues
items: Tolerance/withdrawal not required; physiologic adaptation during prescribed use alone does not establish disorder
Stimulant withdrawal: fatigue, hypersomnia, depression and craving; assess suicide risk
Cannabis withdrawal: irritability, anxiety, insomnia and reduced appetite after sustained use
Caffeine withdrawal: diffuse headache 12–48 h after stopping intake, including NPO surgery; normal neurologic exam

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Reward learning and neuroadaptation strengthen cue-driven behavior while impairing control
Cocaine blocks monoamine reuptake; amphetamines increase release; cannabinoids act mainly at CB1 receptors
THC lipophilic, adipose-stored: urine positive for weeks in chronic use; other drugs clear in days

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **≥2 of 11 DSM-5 criteria in 12 months**; severity **mild 2–3, moderate 4–5, severe ≥6**
Control/social: larger/longer use, failed cutdown, time spent, craving, role failure, social problems, abandoned activities
Risk/pharmacologic: hazardous use, continued despite physical/psychological harm, tolerance, withdrawal
Clinical interview establishes disorder; urine drug testing documents exposure, not severity or current impairment
Screen co-occurring depression, psychosis, HIV/hepatitis risk and polysubstance use; confirm unexpected immunoassay positives

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Motivational interviewing**: explore ambivalence, elicit personal goals, support autonomy; avoid confrontation
★ Stimulant disorder → **contingency management**, CBT/community reinforcement; no FDA-approved maintenance drug
Cannabis disorder → motivational enhancement, CBT and contingency management; no established approved medication
Peer/12-step programs as adjuncts; tailor outpatient versus residential intensity to safety/support and impairment
Stimulant agitation → benzodiazepines/cooling; uncomplicated cannabis intoxication, mild paranoia → observe, no drugs

rows.label: Complications
items: Cocaine/amphetamine → MI, stroke, arrhythmia, psychosis; chronic methamphetamine → cardiomyopathy and dental injury
Cannabis → impaired driving, hyperemesis (cessation, fluids, capsaicin/haloperidol), anxiety or psychosis
Stimulant crash can precipitate severe depression/suicidality; withdrawal usually lacks alcohol-like autonomic danger
Older adults: new benzodiazepine (temazepam) → subacute ataxia, dysarthria, confusion, falls

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Harm reduction: **naloxone** for possible opioid contamination, avoid using alone, offer fentanyl testing access
Treat comorbid illness, relapse planning, overdose education and regular follow-up; recurrence prompts reassessment
Adolescent experimentation without impairment → counsel teen and family; no formal treatment program

rows.label: Mimics
items: Bipolar mania: episodes persist independently of intoxication
Primary psychosis: symptoms outside substance exposure periods
ADHD: longstanding childhood-onset pattern, not episodic intoxication

substance-use-disorders.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [ASAM/AAAP stimulant guideline 2024](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11105801/); DSM-5 criteria established definitions.

table.title: Intoxication by substance
rows: Mydriasis, hypertension, hyperreflexia, paranoia, pressured speech
Violent agitation, hyperthermia; formication with excoriations; MDMA empathic
Red conjunctivae, dry mouth, tachycardia, hunger, slowed time
**Nystagmus**, analgesia, hypertension, myoclonus; violent-catatonic fluctuation, mutism
Perioral/perinasal rash, solvent odor, ataxia/slurring; clears <1 hour
Coma, apnea, hypotension, bradycardia, sluggish pupils

suicide-risk-assessment.name: Suicide risk assessment
suicide-risk-assessment.scope: Risk and protective factors, lethal means restriction, hospitalization criteria, safety planning
suicide-risk-assessment.core: Assess current suicidal intent, plan, access, past behavior, and ability to remain safe; imminent danger requires immediate protection.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prior attempt strongest historical predictor; depression, bipolar disorder, psychosis, substance use, chronic pain
Recent loss, isolation, incarceration/discharge, agitation, hopelessness, firearm access; older men have high fatality risk

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Plan + intent + available lethal means**, preparations, or recent attempt → high acute risk
Command hallucinations, intoxication, severe insomnia, impulsivity, inability to collaborate increase concern
Giving away possessions or sudden calm after despair can signal resolved intent

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Acute distress, impaired judgment, and accessible lethal methods can convert transient suicidal urges into fatal acts
Protective connections and restricted means increase time and opportunity for intervention

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Ask directly** about ideation, intent, plan, timing, access, prior attempts; asking does not induce suicide
Depression or hopelessness, even with somatic complaints → assess suicide risk **before further medical workup**
Assess depression/mania, psychosis, substance use, violence risk, medical contributors, collateral information
Use structured instruments to support assessment, never as a sole disposition rule
Intoxicated patient → observation and reassessment when clinically sober; initial denial is insufficient

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Imminent danger → **constant observation, remove hazards, emergency psychiatric evaluation/hospitalization**
Voluntary admission preferred; involuntary protection if serious danger and refusal, following local law
Treat poisoning/injury first; address agitation, withdrawal, mood/psychotic disorder and underlying medical illness
Low acute risk with reliable support → outpatient care only with collaborative plan and rapid follow-up

rows.label: Complications
items: Fatal or repeated attempts, hypoxic injury, disability, caregiver distress
High vulnerability after emergency/inpatient discharge; abrupt loss of contact raises concern

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Safety plan**: warning signs, coping actions, supportive contacts, professional crisis resources, emergency escalation
★ **Lethal means restriction**: secure/remove firearms, limit medication quantities; enlist trusted support
Arrange prompt follow-up and active care linkage; identify reasons for living and dependable supervision

rows.label: Mimics
items: Nonsuicidal self-injury: no intent to die, but future suicide risk still elevated
Passive death wish: no active plan, still warrants full evaluation
Obsessive intrusive harm thoughts: unwanted/ego-dystonic, without desire or intent to act

suicide-risk-assessment.evidence: Not checked online; established clinical suicide-risk assessment and safety-planning principles; detention law varies locally.

syncope.name: Syncope
syncope.scope: Vasovagal / neurocardiogenic syncope, orthostatic syncope, situational syncope, cardiogenic syncope, breath-holding spells, cerebral hypoperfusion workup
syncope.core: Brief loss of consciousness from global cerebral hypoperfusion with rapid spontaneous recovery; identify cardiac danger before labeling an episode reflex-mediated.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Dehydration, blood loss, autonomic dysfunction, diuretics, nitrates, alpha-1 blockers; prolonged standing, heat, fear
Structural heart disease, conduction disease, arrhythmias, family history of sudden death

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Exertional or supine syncope**, palpitations, absent prodrome, cardiac murmur → high-risk cause
Reflex prodrome: nausea, warmth, diaphoresis, tunnel vision; may include brief myoclonic jerks
Situational triggers: urination, coughing, defecation; breath-holding spells follow crying/pain in young children
Shaving, tight collar, head turning + bradycardia → **carotid sinus hypersensitivity**; confirm with carotid sinus massage

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Vasodilation/bradycardia, failed postural compensation, or low cardiac output transiently limits cerebral flow

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Initial **history, examination, orthostatic BP, ECG**; bedside glucose and targeted pregnancy/bleeding evaluation
Orthostasis: systolic fall ≥20 or diastolic ≥10 mm Hg within 3 minutes standing
High-risk → admission/monitoring; suspected structural disease → echo; intermittent arrhythmia → ambulatory ECG
Tilt-table testing for recurrent unexplained reflex/orthostatic cases; no routine head CT, EEG, carotid ultrasound
Typical breath-holding spells: normal development, awake trigger, rapid recovery; CBC/ferritin and ECG when evaluating

rows.label: Tx
